[Order Explorer](/Feats.aspx?ID=4718) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Druid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=583" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 129 <sup>2.0</sup>

</column>

---

You have learned the secrets of another druidic order, passing whatever rites of initiation that order requires and gaining access to its secrets. Choose an order other than your own. You gain a 1st-level feat that lists that order as a prerequisite, and you are now a member of that order for the purpose of meeting feat prerequisites. If you commit acts anathema to your new order, you lose all feats and abilities requiring that order but retain your other druid feats and abilities. You don’t gain any of the other benefits of the order you chose.

**Special** You can take this feat multiple times. Each time you do, you must choose a different order other than your own.
name: Order Explorer

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 70 <sup>2.1</sup>

**Archetype** [Ostilli Host](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=222)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) or Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)

**Access**
surki ancestry

</column>

---

You've bonded with an attached symbiote known as an ostilli. You can bond with only one ostilli at a time since the symbiote emits low-frequency magical pulses that repel other ostillis. You become trained in [Ostilli Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41); if you were already trained, you become an expert.

 The ostilli is a Tiny creature [grafted](/Rules.aspx?ID=3275) to your body. Like other grafts, it has no Hit Points or Speeds of its own and can't be targeted separately. It can't be removed and dies when you do; in the event of your demise and resurrection, you can bond to a new ostilli during a week of downtime, though you lose any abilities granted by your ostilli bond during that time. Your ostilli is obvious, unless you attempt to cover it with clothing or armor. In such a case, an onlooker can determine you're bonded to an ostilli with a successful [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), Perception, or Surki Lore check against your [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) DC. Your ostilli must be visible for you to use any of the actions it grants.

 Your ostilli is constantly siphoning ambient magic from the surroundings, granting you the Repel Ambient Magic and Spit Ambient Magic actions.

 **Repel Ambient Magic** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) Your ostilli glows green as it absorbs magic. Until the start of your next turn, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC and saving throws against the next [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) attack, cantrip, or spell that targets you. This bonus increases to +2 at 12th level.

 **Spit Ambient Magic** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** Your ostilli flashes red as it regurgitates a dart of magic at a target within 30 feet. This magical dart deals 1d6 piercing damage ([basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC). This damage increases by 1d6 at 6th level and every 4 levels thereafter.
name: Ostilli Host Dedication
prerequisite: Trained in Arcana or Trained in Nature

---

You have delved into the study of the occult and divine, becoming exceptionally skilled at identifying when such forces are at work. Using this esoteric knowledge and your own ingenuity, you have crafted a small charm that soothes your mind and protects you against harm. This charm usually takes the form of a silver chain, a golden scarab, or a withered hand. While you wear this charm, you gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws against mental effects. In addition, you gain the Mystic Aegis reaction. 

 **Mystic Aegis** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Trigger** A creature you have successfully [Recalled Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about would damage you; Requirements You have a free hand; **Effect** You brandish your charm, channeling and shaping the forces within it to protect you against harm. You gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) to all damage equal to 2 + half your level rounded up against the triggering effect.

<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=695" />

---

With your experience as a performer, you can keep a set of medical tools handy at all times. You can wear a [healer's toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2727) as part of any costume or disguise. Creatures will generally only notice the toolkit it if they use a [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) action and succeed at a Perception check against your Performance DC.

 In addition, you can realize at the last moment when you should just be pretending to avoid doing any lasting harm. When you critically fail a Medicine check to [Administer First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=2396), [Treat Disease](/Actions.aspx?ID=2397), [Treat Poison](/Actions.aspx?ID=2398), or [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=2399), you can attempt a Performance check against the patient’s Perception DC. On a success, your critical failure at the Medicine check becomes a failure.
name: Performer's Treatment
prerequisite: Expert in Medicine; Expert in Performance

If you boarded or disembarked from a boat or similar vehicle during this movement, the Strike deals one additional weapon damage die.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 74

**Archetype** [Prophet of Kalistrade](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=315)

**Prerequisites**
trained in [Mercantile Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41); Trained in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47); Charisma +2

**Access**
You’re from Druma.

</column>

---

After induction into the ranks of the Kalistocrats, you learned the skills necessary to succeed in business and rise above others by following a set of detailed strictures. Unless you take measures to hide your affiliation, anyone who has heard of the [Prophets of Kalistrade](/Deities.aspx?ID=23) will know you’re one of them when they see you. You become an expert in Society and can use Society instead of [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) on merchants and traders. 

Additionally, if you don’t already cast spells from spell slots, you learn to cast [spontaneous spells](/Rules.aspx?ID=2224) and gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) activity. You gain a spell repertoire with two common [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) cantrips, plus either [_prestidigitation_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1639) or [_read aura_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1646). You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for these spells is Charisma, and they’re occult spells.
name: Prophet of Kalistrade Dedication

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 290

**Archetype** [Razmiran Priest](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=307)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37); Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38)

</column>

---

You have earned entry to the priesthood of Razmir, either at the Exalted Lodge or another temple where Razmir’s holy masks are forged. You gain a [Razmiri mask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3593) and can [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=2385) a replacement in 4 hours if yours is ever damaged or lost. There is no value in selling your Razmiri mask, and only you gain its benefits. The abilities of your Razmiri mask use the higher of your class DC or spell DC.

You can take the [Cleric Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5066) feat without needing to meet its prerequisites and before you take two other feats from the Razmiran priest archetype, but you must choose [Razmir](/Deities.aspx?ID=357) as your deity. All spells granted by the cleric archetype when gained in this way are [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) spells instead of [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spells, and cleric feats that normally have the [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579) trait instead have the [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662) trait. Your key spellcasting attribute for these spells is Charisma, rather than Wisdom.
name: Razmiran Priest Dedication
prerequisite: Trained in Crafting; Trained in Deception

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 35 --- By channeling your divinity into a creature along with a strike, you can disrupt their ability to recover. The imbued ikon gains the following ability. **Immanence** When you successfully damage an enemy with the ikon, a marking appears around the wound, painted in the red of mortal blood and the gold of divine ichor. When the target would regain Hit Points, such as from a [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623) effect or an ability like [fast healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=62) or [regeneration](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=72), it must attempt a Will save against your class DC to determine the effects, and then the marking fades. The marking otherwise fades after 1 minute. **Success** The creature regains the full number of Hit Points that would be healed.
**Failure** The creature regains only half the number of Hit Points as the contradictory energies swirl within it.
**Critical Failure** The creature doesn’t regain any Hit Points.

    level="1"

>
[Rivethun Emissary Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7571) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 292

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) [Rivethun](/Deities.aspx?ID=388) is a philosophy which characters may choose as their religion. Doing so fulfills the “follower of Rivethun” access condition._

**Archetype** [Rivethun Emissary](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=308)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39); Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)

**Access**
Followers of Rivethun have access to this feat.

</column>

---

You’re a practicing Rivethun emissary, skilled at interacting and bonding with the spirits of living creatures. You become an expert in Diplomacy and Religion. You also gain the Bond with Spirit activity and the [_entreat spirit_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2432) focus spell. If you don’t already have one, you gain a [focus pool](/Rules.aspx?ID=285), which you can regain using the [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=2621) activity to nurture your personal well of spiritual power. Your Rivethun focus spells are [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spells; when you gain this feat, you become trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for Rivethun focus spells is Wisdom.

Bond with Spirit ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [exploration](/Traits.aspx?ID=595)) You can forge a spiritual bond with a creature that is at least friendly toward you or with a terrain that you’re currently in. Forming this bond takes 10 minutes, during which time you must remain adjacent to the creature or within that terrain. If the creature is intelligent, this also requires that creature’s consent, and that intelligent creature can choose to sever this bond with you at any time as a free action, which has the concentrate trait. This bond lasts as long as you are within a mile of the creature or terrain, until you use Bond with Spirit again, or until you make your daily preparations. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 294

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) [Rivethun](/Deities.aspx?ID=388) is a philosophy which characters may choose as their religion. Doing so fulfills the “follower of Rivethun” access condition._

**Archetype** [Rivethun Invoker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=309)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36); Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)

**Access**
Followers of Rivethun have access to this feat.

</column>

---

You’re a practicing Rivethun invoker, able to enter a trance that connects you physically and mentally to surrounding spirits. You become an expert in Athletics and Religion. You also gain the [Diehard](/Feats.aspx?ID=5140) general feat and the Enter Spirit Trance ability. 

**Enter Spirit Trance** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) You enter a self-imposed trance that helps you push the physical limits of your body. You gain a number of temporary Hit Points equal to your level plus your Constitution modifier. The trance lasts for 1 minute, until you fall [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95), or until you [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) it, whichever comes first. While in this trance, you gain a +1 status bonus to Fortitude and Will saving throws and your melee [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) deal 1 additional [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage. Other abilities may require you to be in a spirit trance. When the trace ends, you lose any remaining [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) from Enter Spirit Trance, and you can’t Enter a Spirit Trance for 1 minute.
name: Rivethun Invoker Dedication
prerequisite: Trained in Athletics; Trained in Religion

You land with quick rolls that help you keep your momentum. If you fall and don't take damage (usually due to treating the fall as a shorter distance), you can use your reaction to immediately enter a short roll when you land and [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304). If you are an expert in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34), you can use your reaction to Step or [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) up to half your Speed after you fall and don't take damage. If you're a master in Acrobatics, you can use this reaction to Step or Stride up to your full Speed. If you're legendary in Acrobatics, you don't trigger reactions triggered by movement when you Stride in this way.

[Sanctify Water](/Feats.aspx?ID=6502) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=615" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=695" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 233 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46); you follow a deity with “holy” or “unholy” sanctification

</column>

---

You imbue water with your deity's blessing. Choose a container of water with light Bulk possessed by you or an ally within your reach. Until the end of your next turn, it becomes [holy water](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3001) or [unholy water](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3006). You can choose holy water if your deity allows holy sanctification, unholy water if your deity allows unholy sanctification, or either if your deity allows both sanctifications. This is a temporary effect and doesn't impart monetary value or allow the water to be used for costs of rituals or the like. If you're a master in Religion, you can sanctify two containers when you take this action, and if you're legendary, you can sanctify three.

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 214 1.1 **Archetype** [Scrounger](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=263) **Prerequisites** Trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) --- While others need specialized tools and a dedicated space, you have found a way to build just about anything, anywhere. You can [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=2385) items even without appropriate tools or a workshop. Additionally, you don't need a physical formula book to remember all of your formulas; you pay the same cost as normal to learn them, but you memorize them all. You gain the Cobble Together activity. **Cobble Together** ([exploration](/Traits.aspx?ID=595)) You Craft a [ temporary item](/Rules.aspx?ID=1436) out of anything, anywhere, with whatever materials happen to be on hand, spending only 10 minutes to perform the initial Crafting check. The temporary item must be one you've memorized or have the formula for, and must be common, non-magical, half your level or lower, and must be a weapon, armor, or a non-consumable piece of [ adventuring gear](/Equipment.aspx?Category=1). Instead of a single item, you can create 10 pieces of a single type of ammunition. You can create only the physical item, not any information or magic, so for example, while you could create a blank journal or one with random pages, you couldn't use it as a [scholarly journal](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2763) or a [religious text](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2746).
An item you Cobble Together is a shoddy item, but when creating it you can choose one creature to build it specifically for. That creature doesn't take the normal penalty for using this [ shoddy item](/Rules.aspx?ID=2162). Your temporary item lasts for 1d4 hours before falling apart into its raw components; the GM rolls the number of hours secretly.
name: Scrounger Dedication

<traits>

<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Class" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=397" />

</column>

---

As you work to understand the connection with your missing patron, it’s increasingly easy to form bonds with those around you. Raw magical energy spills easily through the connection but, without a patron’s control, it sometimes resists your demands for it to form proper spells.

You gain the [Witch’s Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=5003) feat, but can’t choose your [familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=5024) or another creature with the [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=653) trait as a charge. When you [cast](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) or [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) [_manifest will_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2147), as long as your charge is within 30 feet, you can choose to center the spell’s [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) on your charge instead of yourself.
name: Seneschal Witch Dedication

[Sentinel Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6409) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 215 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Archetype** [Sentinel](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=264)

</column>

---

You have trained carefully to maximize the protective qualities of your armor. You become trained in light armor and medium armor. If you already were trained in light armor and medium armor, you gain training in heavy armor as well. Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in any type of armor (but not unarmored defense), you also gain that proficiency in the armor types granted to you by this feat. If you have a class feature that grants you expert proficiency in unarmored defense and you're 13th level or higher, you also become an expert in the armor types granted to you by this feat.
name: Sentinel Dedication

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=615" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=695" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 233 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48)

</column>

---

You have learned special tricks that help you follow individuals without them noticing you. When you attempt a Stealth check to [Avoid Notice](/Actions.aspx?ID=2622) while following a specific target, the target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to their Perception DC. If you have master proficiency in Stealth, the penalty is –3 or –4 if you're legendary. If you start an encounter with the target while shadowing them, the target takes this penalty to their initiative roll and to their Perception DC to determine if they notice you, as normal for Sneak.
name: Shadow Mark

<trait label="Press" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=133" />

</column>

---

While your opponent is still recovering from your prior attack, you snag its armor, clothing, or flesh to move it as you please. Make a melee Strike with a finesse weapon or polearm. If you hit a target that is your size or smaller, you can automatically Reposition it, with the same benefits as the Reposition action (including the critical success effect, if your Strike was a critical hit). If you used a weapon with reach, use the weapon’s reach for this Reposition.

This Strike has the following failure effect.

**Failure** The target becomes [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the end of your current turn.

[Smoke Bomb](/Feats.aspx?ID=5770) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Additive" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=795" />
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=812" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 64 <sup>1.1</sup>

</column>

---

You can add a tarry additive to an alchemical bomb to make it emit smoke. When thrown, in addition to its normal effects, the bomb creates a cloud of smoke in a 10-foot burst. You choose which corner of the target's space (or the space in which the bomb lands) the cloud is centered on. Creatures within that area have the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) condition, and all other creatures are concealed to them. The smoke lasts for 1 minute or until dissipated by a strong wind.
name: Smoke Bomb

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 216 1.1 **Archetype** [Snarecrafter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=265) **Prerequisites** Trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) --- You have studied the art of crafting [snares](/Traits.aspx?ID=809) and laying traps, and few have shown more talent in these arts than you. You gain the [Snare Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=843) feat. When you set a snare, the DC of any saving throw it requires uses the higher of your class DC or the snare's DC. If a snare normally takes 1 minute to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=2385), you can Craft it with 3 Interact actions instead.
Each day during your daily preparations, you can prepare four snares from your formula book for quick deployment (increasing to six snares if you're a master in Crafting and eight if you're legendary). Snares prepared in this way don't cost you any resources to Craft.
When you increase your proficiency rank in Crafting to expert, master, or legendary, add three additional snare formulas to your formula book. The snares must be of your level or lower. **Special** Rangers can adapt snare crafting techniques to create snares from natural materials. If you are a ranger, you can use [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) instead of Crafting for all prerequisites and functions of feats from this archetype. (This includes using Survival to Craft a snare.)
name: Snarecrafter Dedication

[Solid Lead](/Feats.aspx?ID=5945) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=818" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 108 <sup>1.1</sup>

</column>

---

Sometimes your case splinters into smaller mysteries, but you never lose sight of the big picture. Once per day when you give up on the subject of a lead due to using [Pursue a Lead](/Actions.aspx?ID=2811) again, you can designate the lead you stopped pursuing as your solid lead for the day. Even though you stopped following the solid lead, you can change back to your solid lead any number of times by using a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait. Doing so ends one of your current leads as normal.

 During your next daily preparations, you can maintain your solid lead or you can remove it; removing it allows you to designate a new solid lead later that day.
name: Solid Lead

---

Choose a bloodline. You become trained in the bloodline’s two skills; for each of these skills in which you were already trained, you become trained in a skill of your choice.

You cast spells like a sorcerer. You gain access to the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) activity. You gain a spell repertoire with two common cantrips from the spell list associated with your bloodline, from the spells granted by your bloodline, or any other cantrips of that tradition you learn or discover. You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for sorcerer archetype spells is Charisma, and they are sorcerer spells of your bloodline’s tradition. You don’t gain any other abilities from your choice of bloodline.
name: Sorcerer Dedication

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 234 1.1 **Prerequisites** Expert in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) --- You spread rumors, which may or may not be true, about a specific subject. If the subject of your rumor is not currently the subject of any contradictory rumors, this takes as long as it would normally take you to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=2391) (typically 2 hours), at the end of which the GM rolls a secret Deception check against a DC they set to see how well you spread the rumor. If your rumor matches any current rumors about the subject, it takes less time to spread, and if you are attempting to overtake a particularly popular and contradictory rumor, it takes much longer or may be impossible. The DC similarly increases or decreases depending on how plausible your rumor is. For example, it might be harder to sow a rumor that the beloved, generous mayor is the head of a cult of murderous demon worshippers. **Critical Success** Your rumor spreads like wildfire. Anyone who succeeds at a check to Gather Information on the specific subject learns your rumor in preference to other rumors about the subject. Your rumor persists for 1 month. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Deception, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39), and [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks in an appropriate situation when you invoke your rumor.
**Success** You successfully spread the rumor. Anyone who succeeds at a check to Gather Information on the specific subject adds your rumor to the list of rumors they could learn about the subject. Your rumor persists for 1 week. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Deception, Diplomacy, and Intimidation checks in an appropriate situation when you invoke your rumor.
**Failure** Your rumor dies off, never becoming popular enough for other people to learn it via Gather Information.
**Critical Failure** You are unable to spread a rumor and take a –4 circumstance penalty to Deception checks to Sow Rumors about the same subject within the same region for 1 week. In addition, a rumor spreads about someone trying to spread false rumors about the subject.
name: Sow Rumor

---

By touching the [_splinter of finality_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3772) in your neck, you conjure a _spectral dagger_ into your hand that resembles the splinter wrapped in a crude hilt. This weapon acts like a [_+1_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840) [_dagger_](/Weapons.aspx?ID=358), and each successful [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with it deals 1 additional [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage. If the attack is a critical hit, this damage increases to 1d6. If the _spectral dagger_ ever leaves your hand, it vanishes and you must spend an action to conjure it again. If this occurs as the result of you making a ranged thrown Strike with the dagger, you resolve the attack before the weapon vanishes.

You can increase the power of your _spectral dagger_ with runes like you can other weapons, transferring the rune from a runestone or other weapon by meditating over the rune as a downtime activity that takes 1 day.

[Spirit Warrior Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7020) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 92

**Archetype** [Spirit Warrior](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=274)

**Access**
Tian Xia orign

</column>

---

You’re a warrior who trains your spirit and body to work in perfect harmony, enhancing your attacks with your spiritual energy while fighting with a ferocious martial technique that combines blade and fist. The damage die for your fist changes to 1d6 instead of 1d4, and your fist gains the [parry](/Traits.aspx?ID=667) trait. You don’t take the normal –2 circumstance penalty when making a lethal attack with your fist or any other unarmed attacks. You gain the Overwhelming Combination action.

**Activate—Overwhelming Combination** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([flourish](/Traits.aspx?ID=606))   **Requirements** You’re wielding a one-handed melee weapon or a melee weapon with the agile or finesse trait; **Effect** Make two [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) against a target within your reach, one with the required weapon and one with your fist [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) attack. If both hit the same target, combine their damage for the purposes of its [resistances](/Rules.aspx?ID=2893) and weaknesses. Apply your multiple attack penalty to each Strike normally.
name: Spirit Warrior Dedication

    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Spiritual Expansion Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=7126) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Animist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=836" />
<trait label="Apparition" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=837" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 24

</column>

---

Your apparitions manifest to scatter the energy of your spell. If the next action you use is to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) that has an area of a [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385), [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386), or [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388) and does not have a duration, increase the area of that spell. Add 5 feet to the radius of a burst that normally has a radius of at least 10 feet (a burst with a smaller radius is not affected). Add 5 feet to the length of a cone or line that is normally 15 feet long or smaller, and add 10 feet to the length of a larger cone or line. 

You can also use this feat to increase the radius of an [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) spell with a duration by 5 feet by dedicating your primary apparition to maintaining the spellshape; dedicating the apparition to the spell prevents you from using the apparition’s vessel spell, apparition skills, or avatar form for the duration of the modified spell.
name: Spiritual Expansion Spell

[Starlit Sentinel Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7033) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 94

**Archetype** [Starlit Sentinel](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=275)

</column>

---

You’ve been chosen by one of the constellations of the Tian Xia zodiac. You gain a transformation seal: a mundane-seeming item of light Bulk, such as a ring, brooch, or key, that has the [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534) trait. If your seal is ever lost or destroyed, you can gain a replacement by spending 1 week of downtime in introspection to reconnect with your constellation. You, and only you, can transform into your sentinel form by Activating the seal.

**Activate—Starlit Transformation** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** Light swirls around you, transforming your armor, clothing, and a single weapon in your possession into a specific alternate outfit. While your equipment might look dramatically different, it functions as normal. If someone attempts to discern your identity, they must use a [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) action to attempt a [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2298) check against your [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) DC, as if you were using the [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) action. Your Deception DC against such attempts is 20 + your proficiency modifier instead of the normal DC. Unlike with Impersonate, you don’t have to attempt a Deception check to interact with someone to conceal your identity—a check happens only if someone else specifically tries to uncover it. You remain in your sentinel form for 10 minutes or until you use Starlit Transformation again to change back to your normal form. 

While you're in sentinel form, your transformed weapon shines with starlight and gains a +1 status bonus to damage rolls with the weapon. You can fling bolts of starlight from your weapon with a Strike action, using your melee attack modifier with the weapon. These bolts deal 1d4 force damage, have a range of 60 feet, are affected by your weapon runes, and have the [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534) and [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=610) traits.
name: Starlit Sentinel Dedication

Your companion is an integral part of your story, and you can expend your mythic power to protect it, defying events that would prevent it from being so. >
[Swarmkeeper Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5463) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 72 <sup>2.1</sup>

**Archetype** [Swarmkeeper](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=223)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)

</column>

---

Your body has become a symbiotic hive for a swarm of crawling insects. You can emit your swarm using the Swarm Forth action, and you can use the Bite and Sting action while your swarm is outside your body to command it to attack. Your deep connection to your swarm precludes you from also having an animal companion, though if an ability allows you to have more than one animal companion (such as the beastmaster archetype), you can count your swarm as one. You're immune to any damage from your swarm, and during your daily preparations you can anoint up to five willing creatures with a concoction made from your pheromones to grant them immunity as well.

 While outside your body, your swarm is Large and has a Speed of 15 feet and a climb Speed of 15 feet. It can occupy the same space as other creatures. While outside your body, the swarm can be attacked. It uses your statistics for defenses but is immune to [grappled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77), [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88), [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90), and [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects that target only a specific number of creatures. The swarm has resistance equal to your level to physical damage and weakness equal to your level to area and splash damage. Any damage that would be dealt to the swarm is dealt to you instead, though you take damage only once from any ability that includes both you and the swarm in the area of effect (though you take the greater amount of damage).

 **Swarm Forth** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Requirements** Your swarm is within your body; **Effect** Your swarm boils forth from your body into a space adjacent to yours. (Its space can overlap yours.) It remains separate from you until the end of your next turn, but you can Sustain the effect up to 1 minute. The effect also ends if you end your turn more than 60 feet away from the swarm. When you use Swarm Forth and each time you Sustain the effect, you can have the swarm Stride.

 When Swarm Forth ends, the swarm disperses into individual creatures. While dispersed, it can no longer be used for actions or be targeted, and the insects return to you and nest in your body again. This typically takes 1 minute unless you're extremely far away (as determined by the GM). 

**Bite and Sting** <actions string="Single Action" /> **Requirements** Your swarm is outside your body; **Effect** Each creature in your swarm's space takes 1d4 piercing damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. At 4th level and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d4.
name: Swarmkeeper Dedication

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 217 1.1 **Archetype** [Talisman Dabbler](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=266) --- You are trained in the use of [talismans](/Equipment.aspx?Category=15&Subcategory=19) and similar magical paraphernalia. This training might have occurred in a formal classroom or been an accumulation of folk magic picked up over time. You can craft talismans and know the formulas for all common talismans of your level or lower. You remember talisman formulas and don't need a formula book for them.
Additionally, you carry a vast collection of magical baubles you can turn into temporary talismans. Each day during your daily preparations, you can make two talismans with an item level no higher than half your level. You must know each talisman's formula. A talisman created this way is a temporary item and loses its magic the next time you make your daily preparations if you haven't already used it. Any saving throw DC required by a temporary talisman you create uses the highest of your class DC, spell DC, or the talisman's DC.
Finally, when you [Affix a Talisman](/Actions.aspx?ID=2632), you can (in any combination) affix or remove up to four talismans in the 10-minute span.
name: Talisman Dabbler Dedication

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 172

**Archetype** [Ulfen Guard](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=320)

**Prerequisites**
member of the Ulfen Guard; Trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36); Trained in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40)

**Access**
At least one of your parents is Ulfen.

</column>

---

Central to your Ulfen Guard training is the ability to protect an ally. You gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) skill feat for [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41). If you were already trained in Warfare Lore, you also become trained in a Lore skill of your choice. You gain the Designate Ally action.

It’s anathema for you to abandon your designated ally or allow your designated ally to die when you can prevent it. If you violate this anathema, you lose the ability to Designate Ally and any feats that use this ability until you spend 1 day of downtime reaffirming your dedication to your allies. 

**Designate Ally** <actions string="Single Action" /> Choose an ally you can see, who becomes your designated ally. For the next minute, whenever your designated ally is adjacent to you and you’re conscious, they gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC and Reflex saving throws. You can have only one designated ally at a time, and if you designate a new ally, the previous ally loses any benefits.
name: Ulfen Guard Dedication
prerequisite: member of the Ulfen Guard; Trained in Athletics; Trained in Intimidation

</column>

---

Your medical training extends to less obvious conditions. When you succeed against a DC 20 check to Treat Wounds, you can also reduce the value of one clumsy, enfeebled, or stupefied condition on the patient by 1. If you’re able to treat more than one creature at once, choose only one to gain this benefit. A creature can benefit from Unusual Treatment only once per day.

If the condition results from an affliction, the affliction isn’t cured, though the condition is reduced as long as the affliction remains at that stage.

If you are a master in Medicine, add the drained condition to the list of conditions you can remove if you succeed at a DC 30 check. If you are legendary in Medicine, you reduce the chosen condition by 2 instead of by 1.
name: Unusual Treatment

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />

<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 183 <sup>2.0</sup>

**Archetype** [Ursine Avenger Hood](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=200)

</column>

---

You draw the _[Ursine Avenger Hood](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2368)_ over your head and its fur over your arms, assuming an ursine form that has traits of your original form as well as that of a bear. In your ursine form, you gain a jaws [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack that deals 1d8 piercing damage and a claws unarmed attack that deals 1d6 slashing damage and has the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170) trait. Both unarmed attacks are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group. You lose the ability to speak complex sentences while transformed and can only communicate through grunts and gestures; this prevents you from using effects that require a shared or spoken language until you revert back to your non-hybrid form. You can use this action while transformed to remove the hood and return to your original form.
name: Ursine Avenger Form

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Wardens of Wildwood</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #201: Pactbreaker](/Sources.aspx?ID=241) pg. 79

**Archetype** [Verduran Shadow](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=312)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48); Trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49)

</column>

---

Your awareness of primal energies allows you to explore forests with preternatural ease. You become an expert in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49). You can substitute your proficiency in Survival for your proficiency in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) when meeting feat prerequisites and gaining additional benefits from feats for being an expert, master, or legendary in Stealth; however, unless you also fulfill the Stealth prerequisite, you can only use those feats in forest terrain. While in forests, you can use your Survival modifier in place of your Stealth modifier when you [Avoid Notice](/Actions.aspx?ID=2622), [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404), [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405), or would use Stealth to roll initiative.

**Special** You can’t select another dedication feat until you’ve gained two other feats from the Verduran Shadow archetype.
name: Verduran Shadow Dedication
prerequisite: Trained in Stealth; Trained in Survival

<title
    level="1"

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Vigilante Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6424) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 218 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Archetypes** [Vigilante](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=267), [Gray Gardener](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=124) (Level 2)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38)

</column>

---

You have two identities, each with its own name and abilities. Your social identity is an upstanding member of society, while your vigilante identity is a skilled and cunning warrior. Neither of these identities is a false front; you really are both of these people. If someone attempts to discern your other identity, they must use a [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) action to attempt a Perception check against your Deception DC, as if you were using the [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) action. Your Deception DC against such attempts is 20 + your proficiency modifier instead of the normal DC. Unlike with Impersonate, you don't have to attempt a Deception check to interact with someone to conceal your other identity—a check happens only if someone else specifically tries to uncover your other identity. 

Changing from one identity to the other takes 1 minute and must be done out of sight from other creatures. As this process involves both physical changes such as clothing and makeup, along with an altered state of mind, other effects that change your appearance don't reduce the time required to change identities. 

Your two identities are completely distinct. Checks to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about one of your identities don't reveal information about the other unless the person attempting the check knows both identities are the same person. Effects that detect you based on your identity work only if you are currently in the identity the effect is trying to detect; otherwise, the effect fails as if the target didn't exist. 

To maintain the separation between your identities, some of your abilities have the [vigilante](/Traits.aspx?ID=803) trait. Your class feats and vigilante feats are associated with your vigilante identity, and using them while in your social identity may risk exposing you as a vigilante. If your identity is exposed to the public, you lose the benefits of Vigilante Dedication to disguising yourself, but you can spend 1 week of downtime to create a new social identity.
name: Vigilante Dedication

[Wandering Chef Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7053) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 100

**Archetype** [Wandering Chef](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=277)

</column>

---

Whether trained in a noble kitchen or a humble home, you know how to cook delicious dishes and source ingredients from the wilderness or urban settings. You become trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37); if you were already trained in Crafting, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You can use [cookware](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2717) instead of an [alchemist’s toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2702) to craft alchemical foods. When using the [Subsist](/Actions.aspx?ID=2368) downtime activity, you can use Crafting or Cooking [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) in place of [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49), and if you roll a failure, you get a success instead.

You gain the [Quick Alchemy](/Actions.aspx?ID=2801) benefits, but can use it only to create [consumables](/Rules.aspx?ID=2951), and the consumables must be [alchemical food](/Rules.aspx?ID=1905). Any items you choose with Alchemical Crafting must be alchemical food, but they can be 1st level or 2nd level instead of only 1st level. 

You create up to 4 [versatile vials](/Classes.aspx?ID=56) during your daily preparations. Typically, a wandering chef’s versatile vials take the form of parcels of foraged ingredients.
name: Wandering Chef Dedication

>
[Waterfowl Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=7495) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=656" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=701" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=732" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 80

**Prerequisites**
[Monastic Weaponry](/Feats.aspx?ID=5979)

</column>

---

In your hands, swords dance like rainfall over the waves; who can tell where the storm ends and the sea begins? Developed by Swordmaster Ganhil to compete with the House of Untwisting Iron, this stance integrates fluid swordplay into even the simplest movements.

 While in Waterfowl Stance, the dandpatta, scimitar, talwar, and zulfikar gain the monk trait for you. When you [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=2370) a creature’s space or [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298) over a creature while wielding one of these weapons, you can deal that creature 1d6 slashing damage. This damage is increased to 2d6 if the weapon has a _[greater striking rune](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829)_ and 3d6 if it has a _[major striking rune](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829)._
name: Waterfowl Stance

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 81

**Requirements**
You’ve spent at least 1 minute in mutual conversation with a creature.

</column>

---

Your ability to discern information about those you interact with is without peer. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) to gain a [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) skill specific to the required creature for the next 24 hours; you have mythic proficiency with that skill and can use it to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about the creature, [Decipher Writings](/Actions.aspx?ID=2363) created by the creature, [Earn Income](/Actions.aspx?ID=2364) or [Subsist](/Actions.aspx?ID=2368) in areas ruled by the creature, or perform other appropriate tasks as determined by the GM.

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 76 2.1 **Archetype** [Werecreature](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=225) **Requirements** You were born into a lineage of true werecreatures or were afflicted with the curse of the werecreature. --- You're a werecreature, able to shift between your humanoid shape, an animal shape, and a monstrous hybrid of the two. You gain the beast and werecreature traits. Choose your werecreature type from the table below. Once chosen, this can't be changed. You gain the [Toughness](/Feats.aspx?ID=5227) feat but also a weakness to [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=379) equal to half your level. You gain the Change Shape action. On the night of the full moon, you automatically use Change Shape to assume your hybrid shape, and you can't voluntarily activate or dismiss Change Shape until sunrise. **Change Shape** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Effect** You transform into your hybrid or animal shape. Your equipment transforms with you and continues to provide bonuses, but your animal shape cannot use weapons, shields, or other held items and cannot use [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) actions. You gain a movement speed, unarmed attacks, and potentially other abilities based on your werecreature type. These unarmed attacks are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group. You can Dismiss the effect to return to your humanoid shape, and you resume your humanoid shape automatically if you're reduced to 0 Hit Points. ## Werecreature Types

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Wild Mimic Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5515) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 80 <sup>2.1</sup>

**Archetype** [Wild Mimic](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=226)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)

</column>

---

Fighting in the wilds has honed your understanding of the unique abilities many creatures have. You're trained in [Wild Mimic Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41), a special Lore skill that can be used only to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about creatures to learn their abilities. If you have legendary proficiency in Nature, you gain expert proficiency in Wild Mimic Lore, but you can't increase your proficiency in Wild Mimic Lore by any other means. When you succeed at a Wild Mimic Lore to Recall Knowledge, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your saving throws against the next attack or ability that the subject of your Recall Knowledge targets you with.
name: Wild Mimic Dedication

---

You cast spells like a witch. Choose a patron; you gain a [familiar](/Rules.aspx?ID=2121) with two common cantrips of your choice from your chosen patron's tradition, but aside from the tradition, you don't gain any other effects the patron would usually grant. Your familiar gains the normal number of abilities for a familiar instead of those a witch familiar normally gets. 

You gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2718) activity. You can prepare one cantrip each day from your familiar. You're trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for witch archetype spells is Intelligence, and they are witch spells of your patron's tradition. You become trained in the skill associated with the patron's tradition; if you were already trained in it, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice
name: Witch Dedication

</column>

---

You cast spells like a wizard, gaining a spellbook with four common arcane cantrips of your choice. You gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2718) activity. You can prepare two cantrips each day from your spellbook. You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for wizard archetype spells is Intelligence, and they are arcane wizard spells. You become trained in Arcana; if you were already trained in Arcana, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. Select a school; you don’t gain any abilities from your choice of school, but qualify for feats as a member.
name: Wizard Dedication

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the Worm Caller archetype.

Your training in the wrestling arts has made you particularly adept at moving, striking, and grappling while unencumbered. You become an expert in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) and gain the [Titan Wrestler](/Feats.aspx?ID=5226) skill feat. You don’t take the –2 circumstance penalty for making a lethal attack with your nonlethal unarmed attacks. In addition, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude DC when resisting an opponent’s attempts to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) you or Swallow you Whole.

You’re primed to face off against threats from the [Outer Rifts](/Planes.aspx?ID=45). You gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) skill feat for [Demon Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41). If you were already trained in Demon Lore, you also become trained in a Lore skill of your choice. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to initiative rolls in encounters against [fiends](/Traits.aspx?ID=600), and if you tie with a fiend’s initiative roll, you go first. 

Certain wylderheart feats give you focus spells. The rules for focus spells appear [here](/Rules.aspx?ID=2228). When you gain your first wylderheart focus spell, you become trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for the wylderheart archetype spells is Wisdom, and they’re [primal](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=4) spells. You can Refocus by celebrating life or spending time in nature.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=615" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 231 <sup>1.1</sup>

</column>

---

You can hastily patch damaged equipment together, but the temporary fix lacks the full care required for lasting repairs. You patch together a broken item possessed by you or an adjacent willing creature. Until the item takes damage again, it still functions as a [shoddy](/Rules.aspx?ID=2162) item of its type. If it's a magic item or another item with activations, it can't be activated while patched together, but can be used for normal functions (such as [Striking](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with a weapon or using [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) with a shield). This activity restores no Hit Points, so the item is easy to [destroy](/Rules.aspx?ID=2160) . Once the item is [Repaired](/Actions.aspx?ID=2384) normally such that it is no longer [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=60), it is also no longer shoddy.
name: Improvised Repair

    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Ambush Bladderwort](/Feats.aspx?ID=4296) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Composite" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=501" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Plant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=125" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 36 <sup>2.0</sup>

</column>

---

You plant the seed of a giant bladderwort in an unoccupied square of ground or water within 30 feet. It lasts for 10 minutes. Using this impulse again ends any previous one. If a creature enters its square, the seed erupts into a voluminous, translucent plant that seals tight around the triggering creature and fills with water. Unless the creature succeeds at a Reflex save against your class DC, it's [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) within the bladderwort and must hold its breath or begin [drowning](/Rules.aspx?ID=468). The [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) DC is also your class DC. The plant has AC 10 and 50 Hit Points.

 If a creature dies inside it, the plant shrinks down, converting itself and the remains into a watery fruit. A creature can eat this consumable to regain 1d8+4 HP, after which that creature is temporarily immune for 10 minutes. This fruit rots after 1 hour.

---
**Level (+4)** The bladderwort's HP increase by 25 and the fruit's healing increases by 1d8+4.
name: Ambush Bladderwort

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />

**Archetype** [Kitharodian Actor](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=301)

</column>

---

You participated in a performance of _The Leaping Lion_, a play focusing on Cyricas, the animal-loving adventurer who traveled with his ape friend Mardu and remains a favorite hero among Taldan youth. You become trained in Nature and a Lore skill related to a particular type of animal commonly used in show business (such as Canine Lore, Ursine Lore, or Primate Lore); if you were already trained in either, you become an expert in that skill instead. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to all checks to [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400) and [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about creatures with the animal trait. You can use your chosen animal Lore to Command an Animal of that type.

Your arcane legacy allows you to perceive how magic affects everything. You become trained in one skill of your choice. Additionally, you can use arcane arts to tinker with your selection of spells. During your daily preparations, you can choose one spell in your spell repertoire to be a signature spell that day. You can use the [Learn a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2366) activity to add more arcane spells to the list you choose from, but if you prepare a spell that isn't in your repertoire, you temporarily add it to your repertoire at the spell rank of your choice instead of making it a signature spell.

<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=73" />

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

You rush forward, moving enemies aside to reach your foe. You [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305), attempting to move through your enemies’ spaces. Roll an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check and compare the result to the Fortitude DC of each creature whose space you attempt to move through during your Stride, moving through its space on a success but ending your movement before entering its space on a failure. You can then [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306), regardless of how your Stride ended. You can use Barreling Charge to [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310), [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312), or [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) instead of Stride if you have the corresponding movement type.

If you gain a Focus Pool from any Red Mantis Assassin class feats, you can Refocus by praying to Achaekek or researching your assigned kill.

 You also have access to the [Red Mantis magic school](/ArcaneSchools.aspx?ID=23). In addition to preparing spells from the divine spell list, you can prepare spells from this school. Regardless of their usual magic tradition, when you prepare spells from this school, they are divine spells, as are any Red Mantis focus spells you gain.

---

You adapt a creature to live among the trees, improving its ability to [climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), [balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=2369), and [leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298). ---
**Level (6th)** You can target up to 5 willing creatures.

<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />

You are as at home in the treetops as you are beneath their branches. You gain a [climb Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2349) of 15 feet when moving through trees, vines, and other foliage. You aren’t [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) while Climbing or Balancing on a tree.

prerequisite: Verduran Shadow Dedication; Trained in Athletics

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cleric" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=554" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 116 <sup>2.0</sup>

**Cost**
Expend a harm or heal spell

</column>

---

You siphon the energies of life and death through a melee attack and into your foe. Make a melee Strike. On a hit, you cast the 1-action version of the expended spell to damage the target, in addition to the normal damage from your Strike. The target automatically gets a failure on its save (or a critical failure if your Strike was a critical hit). The spell doesn’t have the manipulate trait when cast this way.

The spell is expended with no effect if your Strike fails or hits a creature that isn’t damaged by that energy type (such as if you hit a non-undead creature with a heal spell).
name: Channel Smite

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=656" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=701" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 121 <sup>1.1</sup>

</column>

---

You enter a tightly coiled stance, with your hands poised as venomous fangs. While in this stance, the only Strikes you can make are cobra fang unarmed attacks. These deal 1d4 piercing damage; are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group; and have the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [deadly d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=570), [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602), [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719), and [venomous](/Traits.aspx?ID=785) traits.

 While in Cobra Stance, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Fortitude saves and your Fortitude DC, and you gain poison resistance equal to half your level.
name: Cobra Stance

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 102 2.0 --- You use a performer’s cold reading techniques, aura reading, and other tricks to discover your foe’s strengths and weaknesses. The GM rolls a secret [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) check for you against the [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) or [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) DC (whichever is higher) of an enemy of your choice who is not [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) from you, [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) from you, or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96) by you, and who is engaged in combat. The GM might apply a penalty for the distance between you and the enemy. The enemy is then temporarily immune to your Combat Reading for 1 day. **Critical Success** The GM chooses and tells you two of the following pieces of information about the enemy: which of the enemy's weaknesses is highest, which of the enemy's saving throws has the lowest modifier, one immunity the enemy has, or which of the enemy's resistances is highest. In the event of a tie, the GM should pick one at random.
**Success** The GM chooses one piece of information from the above list to tell you about the enemy.
**Critical Failure** The GM gives you false information (the GM makes up the information).
name: Combat Reading

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 21 2.0 --- You grasp the animating force within an elemental creature and bend it to your will. Choose a trait matching one of your kinetic elements and target an [elemental](/Traits.aspx?ID=57) creature within 30 feet that has the chosen trait. The elemental becomes [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=6) by you if its level is equal to or lower than your level — 3, or [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) for as long as you Sustain the effect if its level is equal to your level — 2 or higher. It can attempt a Will saving throw against your class DC to resist being controlled by you or to end the slowed effect. If the target is already under someone else's command, it can't be slowed by this ability, and the controlling creature also rolls a saving throw, with the elemental using the better result. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected and is temporarily immune for 24 hours.
**Success** The target is unaffected.
**Failure** The elemental creature is controlled or slowed as long as you Sustain the impulse, up to 1 minute. This effect ends if you or an ally attacks the elemental.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but you can Sustain the impulse up to 1 hour.
name: Command Elemental

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 50 **Archetype** [Eagle Knight](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=314) **Prerequisites** [Eagle Knight Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7666); Expert in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) --- You help an ally shake off any impediment that would give an enemy an unfair advantage. You rally a creature within 30 feet in an attempt to reduce its [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) or [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) condition. If a creature has multiple conditions from this list, choose one. When you’re a master in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39), add [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) and [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) to the list of conditions. When you’re legendary in Diplomacy, add [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) to the list of conditions; if the stunned condition has a duration instead of a value, you can’t use Commitment to Equality to reduce it. Attempt a Diplomacy check against the saving throw DC of the effect that caused the condition; if there was no saving throw DC, use the hard DC for the level of the creature, hazard, or item that caused the effect. You can’t treat a condition that came from an artifact or effect above 20th level unless you’re legendary in Diplomacy; even if you can, the [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) DC increases by 10. You can’t treat a condition that is part of a [curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=566) or [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578) or is a natural state of the target. Once you attempt to treat a target’s condition, that target is immune to further attempts for 1 hour, regardless of the result. **Critical Success** Reduce the condition’s value by 2.
**Success** Reduce the condition’s value by 1.
**Critical Failure** Increase the condition’s value by 1.
name: Commitment to Equality
prerequisite: Eagle Knight Dedication; Expert in Diplomacy

You can squeeze out of tight situations by twisting and bending your body into unnatural positions, gaining an advantage against foes that try to pin you down. You gain the [Quick Squeeze](/Feats.aspx?ID=5199) skill feat, and if you're a master in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34), you can Squeeze at full Speed. Whenever you successfully [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) using Acrobatics, the creature you Escaped from is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) against the next attack you make against it before the end of your next turn.
name: Contortionist

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=534" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 113

**Prerequisites**
[aloof firmament hybrid study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=7); [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755)

**Trigger**
You hit a target with a Spellstrike.

</column>

---

You flow around your foe, using the magic of your attack to carry you away. You [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298), [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377), or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378), and this movement doesn’t trigger reactions from the creature you hit. If you High Jump or Long Jump, you don’t have to perform the initial Stride (nor do you fall if you don’t Stride 10 feet). 

The lightness of your steps persists after the jump, granting you the ability to land on or walk on the surface of water or other liquids until the end of your next turn.
name: Distant Waterbird's Poise

You enhance your spell with elemental water, soaking the target. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell targeting a single creature, you soak the target of the spell with water. If the target has [persistent acid or fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29), the DC to end those conditions is reduced to 10, and the creature can attempt a flat check to end those types of persistent damage immediately. The spell gains the [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165) trait (causing it to deal extra damage to creatures with weakness to water).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=601" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=73" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 143 <sup>2.0</sup>

**Requirements**
You are wielding a one-handed melee weapon and have a free hand

</column>

---

You snap your free hand over to grip your weapon just long enough to add momentum and deliver a more powerful blow to your opponent. Make a Strike with the required weapon. You quickly switch your grip during the Strike in order to make the attack with two hands. If the weapon doesn’t normally have the two-hand trait, increase its weapon damage die by one step for this attack. (Rules on increasing die size appear on page 276.) If the weapon has the two-hand trait, you gain the benefit of that trait and a circumstance bonus to damage equal to the weapon’s number of damage dice. When the Strike is complete, you resume gripping the weapon with only one hand. This action doesn’t end any stance or fighter feat effect that requires you to have one hand free.
name: Dual-Handed Assault

Select one enemy you can see and proclaim a challenge against it. That enemy is your dueling opponent until it's defeated, it flees from the encounter, or the encounter ends. Any time you hit that enemy using a single one-handed melee weapon while your other hand or hands are free, you gain a circumstance bonus to the Strike's damage equal to the number of damage dice your weapon deals.

 If you attack a creature other than your dueling opponent, you take a circumstance penalty to damage equal to the number of damage dice your weapon deals.

You’ve practiced an impressive spin technique with your construct, automatically attacking in tandem as you launch each other through the air. You Command your construct companion to fight alongside you, after which you both [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298) in the same direction, making an unarmed [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) at the start or end of the Leap; this uses your companion’s actions for the turn. If the Strikes both hit the same creature, combine their damage for the purposes of [resistances](/Rules.aspx?ID=2893) and weaknesses.

**Unstable** Function You spin farther and higher, though the extreme movement risks discombobulating your innovation. Add the [unstable](/Traits.aspx?ID=416) trait to Duo Dragon Kick. Increase the distance of your Leaps by 10 feet if horizontal or 5 feet if vertical.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=812" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 64 <sup>1.1</sup>

</column>

---

Thanks to the time you've spent studying and experimenting, you know how to scale your formulas into larger batches that don't require any additional attention. Increase the number of items you can create each day with advanced alchemy to 6 + your Intelligence modifier.

 In addition, when you [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=2385) alchemical consumables during downtime, you can produce twice as many alchemical items in a single batch without spending additional preparatory time. For instance, if you are creating [elixirs of life](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3308), you can craft up to eight elixirs in a single batch using downtime, rather than four. This doesn't change the amount of alchemical reagents or other ingredients required to craft each item, nor does it change your rate of progress for days past the base downtime spent.
name: Efficient Alchemy

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 59 2.0 **Archetype** [Elementalist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=207) **Prerequisites** [Elementalist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=4340); [Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=604) --- Your familiar becomes an elemental spirit capable of taking on aspects of the elements. Other than taking the form of an elemental instead of an animal, this familiar continues to use all the same rules as other familiars. If you want to give your familiar the elemental familiar abilities found on page 42, you must select that familiar ability. Your familiar gains one additional familiar ability each day, which must be one of the following elemental familiar abilities. While your familiar has an elemental familiar ability, your familiar is composed of the associated elemental matter and gains the matching elemental trait. You can't select more than one elemental familiar ability at a time.
  • **Air** If your familiar stays completely still for 1 round, it becomes [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26) until it next takes an action. Any motion, even being moved or carried by another creature, ends this effect.
  • **Earth** Your familiar gains resistance to physical damage (except [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=374)) equal to half your level.
  • **Fire** Your familiar sheds [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 20-foot radius (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) for the next 20 feet) and emits warmth. Creatures who remain within a 15-foot emanation don't take damage from [severe environmental cold](/Rules.aspx?ID=642).
  • **Metal** Your familiar gains resistance to physical damage from metal weapons equal to half your level.
  • **Water** Your familiar can move through a gap at least 2 inches wide without [Squeezing](/Actions.aspx?ID=31) and can Squeeze through a gap at least 1 inch wide.
  • **Wood** If your familiar remains in bright light for 1 round, it gains [fast healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=15) equal to half your level. Once it is out of bright light, this effect ends.
name: Elemental Familiar

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

**Prerequisites**
[Rivethun Emissary Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7571)

</column>

---

You forge a mystical bond with a spirit or create a spirit from a fragment of your own soul. You gain a familiar. If you already have a familiar, you gain the [Enhanced Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=4717) feat.

Your familiar gains two additional [familiar abilities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2125) each day, one of which must be used to select the following master ability.

**Synchronize Spirit** You can synchronize your spiritual energy with that of your familiar to temporarily become part spirit yourself. Once per round, you can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) to synchronize your spirit with that of your familiar. You remain synchronized with your spirit until the beginning of your next turn. While synchronized, whenever you [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) or [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) without a duration that deals damage, you deal spirit damage instead of your normal damage.
name: Emissary Familiar

</traits>

---

You have studied a specific type of wild creature and can hunt it more easily. When you gain this feat, choose animals, beasts, dragons, or both fungi and plants as your favored prey. When you roll initiative and can see an enemy that belongs to the chosen category, you can Hunt Prey as a free action, designating that enemy.

You can use this free action even if you haven’t identified the creature yet with Recall Knowledge. The benefit doesn’t apply against favored enemies disguised as other creatures, and the GM determines whether it applies against a creature disguised as a favored prey

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Swashbuckler" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=825" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 165 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Archetype** [Ulfen Guard](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=320) (Level 8)

**Trigger**
An ally within your melee reach is hit by an attack, you can see the attacker, and a +2 circumstance bonus to AC would turn the critical hit into a hit or the hit into a miss.

**Requirements**
You are wielding a single one-handed melee weapon and have your other hand or hands free.

</column>

---

You use your weapon to deflect the attack against your ally, granting a +2 circumstance bonus to their AC against the triggering attack. This turns the triggering critical hit into a hit, or the triggering hit into a miss. You gain panache until the end of your next turn.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=601" />
<trait label="Ranger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=682" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=687" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=701" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 59

**Requirements**
You are wielding a two-handed [hammer](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=8), [spear](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=14), or [polearm](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=11).

</column>

---

You enter a stance that allows you to leverage the haft of your weapon to brutal effect as an effective and frighteningly efficient weapon in its own right. You treat the haft of your wielded weapon as a simple weapon dealing 1d4 bludgeoning damage. The haft is in the [club](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=5) group and has the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526) and [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602) traits. The haft shares any [fundamental runes](/Rules.aspx?ID=3167) attached to the main weapon, so long as it would normally qualify for them.

While in Haft Striker Stance, you can use feats and abilities that normally require you to be wielding two melee weapons each in a different hand, treating the haft as the second weapon, but you can’t use abilities that require you to be wielding a two-handed weapon.
