[You Don't Smell Right](/Feats.aspx?ID=5502) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 78 <sup>2.1</sup>

**Archetype** [Werecreature](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=225)

**Prerequisites**
[Werecreature Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5486)

</column>

---

You can sniff out fellow werecreatures and master impersonators alike. You gain [scent](/Rules.aspx?ID=417) as an [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) sense with a range of 30 feet or extend the range of your scent by 30 feet. When a creature that's transformed into another form or is [Impersonating](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) a specific creature passes within range of your scent ability, the GM rolls a secret Perception check for you to realize that the creature is transformed, even if you didn't spend an action to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301). When you actively Seek a creature within range of your scent, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Perception check to determine if it's disguised.
name: You Don't Smell Right

[Cling](/Feats.aspx?ID=4451) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Goblin" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=81" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 57 <sup>2.0</sup>

**Requirements**
Your last action was a successful Strike and you have a free hand

</column>

---

You hang onto a foe to harry them into submission. If your target moves while you're hanging onto it, you can choose to move with the target. The target is released if you choose not to move with it, at the start of your next turn, or if the target [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=79). Attempts to Escape from a Cling are made against your Acrobatics DC and follow the rules on page 416, but they end the Cling instead of the conditions normally ended by the Escape action.

**Special** You can use this action without a free hand if your preceding Strike was made with your jaws or a similar unarmed attack you could use to hang on. The GM determines which unarmed attacks apply. Hanging on in this way prevents you from using that unarmed attack.

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 74 --- Tales tell of the Tiger stalking the Mousedeer for days, hidden and instilling dread upon its prey. Your dance embodies the character role so well you can trail an opponent from its own shadow. Attempt a [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) check against the Will DC of a single adjacent enemy. **Critical Success** You step on the foe’s shadow, bringing a cold dread. The opponent is [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 2; its shadow remains pinned underfoot, stretching and deforming to remain connected to your square, and indicates where it has gone even if you lose sight of the foe. The creature can’t reduce its frightened condition below 1 as long as you remain on its shadow. Your connection to its shadow breaks if the distance between you and the target exceeds 120 feet or if you don’t end your turn adjacent to the target. Once your connection to its shadow breaks, the enemy is immune to Dance of the Tiger for 1 hour.
**Success** As critical success, except the creature is only frightened 1 and your connection to its shadow breaks at 60 feet instead of 120.

---

You dart under the legs of your enemies in combat. You can end a successful [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=29) action in a Large or larger enemy's space. Also, when using the [Step Lively](/Feats.aspx?ID=1432) feat, you can [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=87) into the triggering enemy's space. The enemy must have limbs or otherwise leave you enough room for this maneuver, as determined by the GM. For instance, you could share space with a giant or dragon, but not an ooze.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Spore War</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Elf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=58" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #210: Whispers in the Dirt](/Sources.aspx?ID=253) pg. 80

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) or Expert in [Demon Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41)

</column>

---

The [demons](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=387) of Tanglebriar have long haunted your dreams, just as they have long threatened Kyonin. You have not only studied these fiendish foes well, but have trained extensively to battle the hordes of demons that serve [Treerazer](/Deities.aspx?ID=324) and are particularly adept at striking desperate melee blows against them. 

When you make your daily preparations, choose one kind of demon, such as [succubus](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2897), [omox](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2898), [shemhazian](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2900), or Treerazer. For the remainder of the day, the first time you hit one of those specific demons in a round with a melee Strike, you also deal 1d6 additional [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage. At 13th level, the extra damage increases to 2d6 additional spirit damage, and at 17th level, the extra damage increases to 3d6 spirit damage.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Fierce Competitor](/Feats.aspx?ID=5332) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Centaur" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=747" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=647" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 32 <sup>2.1</sup>

**Frequency**
once per day

</column>

---

You challenge a single ally to a physical competition. This competition must involve accomplishing a specific goal for a specific use of the [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) or [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) skill, such as [Climbing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374) to the top of a wall, [Tripping](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382) a specific foe, or [Long Jumping](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378) across a chasm. You and your selected ally gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the associated skill check for 1 minute or until one of you wins the challenge, whichever is first. If you win this competition, you gain a +2 status bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks for 1 hour.
name: Fierce Competitor

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Friendly Fling](/Feats.aspx?ID=5375) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=645" />
<trait label="Minotaur" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=788" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 44 <sup>2.1</sup>

**Requirements**
You are adjacent to an ally.

</column>

---

You can scoop up your friends with your horns to hurl them across the battlefield. Pick up an adjacent willing ally who is smaller than you and toss them to an unoccupied space you can see within 20 feet. Since you are using your horns, you don't need to have any hands free to do this. Your ally's movement doesn't trigger reactions. Your ally ends this movement on their feet and doesn't take damage from the fall but takes 1d6 piercing damage from your horns. If your ally ends this movement within melee reach of at least one enemy, they can make a melee Strike against an enemy within their reach as a reaction.
name: Friendly Fling
requirement: You are adjacent to an ally.
requirement_markdown: You are adjacent to an ally.

---

Your upbringing emphasized teamwork, and helping your allies comes naturally to you. After you [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) an ally at a skill check that doesn’t have the attack trait, you can also Aid any other ally who attempts the same skill check for the same purpose that round. You do so as a free action rather than a reaction.

The preparation you did to help must still apply to the other allies, and you can Aid each ally only once. For example, if you helped lift up an ally to Aid them on an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check to scale a wall, you could keep the same posture to give a boost to other allies attempting to scale the wall in the same round.
name: Group Aid

You grow a simple tool from your own body, coaxing flowers, vines, roots, and wood to grow and sprout from your flesh into the desired shape. You create a one level 0 common simple [tool](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2759) with no intricate parts or written text, such as a [crowbar](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2718), [rope](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2748), or shovel. You can’t replicate a tool kit or weapon with this ability. This item lasts for 1 minute, or until you create another tool with this ability, whichever comes first. When duration runs out, the item crumbles to mulch.

**Special** This feat gains the trait for your ancestry.

You can perform minor mischief with your tail. You can use your tail to Steal an object, though your tail still can’t hold onto it at the end of your action.     right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Life Leap](/Feats.aspx?ID=4434) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gnome" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=80" />
<trait label="Move" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=114" />
<trait label="Teleportation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=156" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 53 <sup>2.0</sup>

**Requirements**
You must be adjacent to a living creature

</column>

---

You phase through a space that a living creature occupies in a flash, spontaneously appearing on the opposite side of it in a vibrant display of colorful light. You move from your current location to another location that's still adjacent to the same living creature, but on the opposite side or corner of the creature's space. To determine whether a position is valid, use the same rules as for flanking: a line through the center of the two spaces must pass through opposite sides or corners of the creature's space.

You pass through the creature's life force, appearing in the selected location; this doesn't trigger reactions based on movement. You must be able to see your destination, and you can't move farther than your Speed would allow.

[Life's Blood](/Feats.aspx?ID=6905) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=623" />
<trait label="Samsaran" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=828" />
<trait label="Vitality" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=509" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 56

</column>

---

Your journey to enlightenment has made your blood possess nigh-immortal properties, allowing you to heal others. You sacrifice some of your vitality to heal another willing living creature that’s adjacent to you, coating its wounds with your blood. You lose 3d6 Hit Points, plus an additional 1d6 Hit Points for every 2 levels you have beyond 10th. This damage can’t be resisted, prevented, or negated in any way. The target creature regains a number of Hit Points equal to the damage you took. Creatures you heal in this manner are then temporarily immune to your Life’s Blood for 24 hours.

Putting on a new face offers a great way to get a fresh perspective on life. When you Change Shape into your everyday form, you gain the effects of a 3rd-rank [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1568) for 1 hour or until you shift back, whichever comes first, except it’s a [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670) effect rather than an [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629). However, your transformations can be broken with a good shock; if you gain the [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) or [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) condition while transformed, your transformation ends, returning you to your tanuki form, and your confidence is so shaken you can’t attempt to resume that specific disguise again until your next daily preparations.

name: Moray Eel Mount

    right="Feat 9"

>
[Rapid Retraining](/Feats.aspx?ID=5258) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Reincarnated" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=783" />
<trait label="Universal Ancestry" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=467" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #199: To Bloom Below the Web](/Sources.aspx?ID=225) pg. 80

</column>

---

Some feel trapped by their choices and have a tough time reinventing themselves. To you, this dilemma is just a natural part of reincarnation. Retraining other feats or skill increases during downtime only takes 4 days instead of a week, and class features that require a choice can be retrained in a week instead of a month. You also never need to find a teacher to retrain, as the memories of abilities you possessed in past lives are superior to any instructor.
name: Rapid Retraining

[River Adaptation](/Feats.aspx?ID=6864) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Lizardfolk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=760" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 45

**Prerequisites**
[Makari Lizardfolk](/Heritages.aspx?ID=378) heritage

</column>

---

Webbing sprouts on your legs and tail as you shift to a more aquatic form. You can cast [_feet to fins_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1525) as an innate divine spell once per day. This innate magic relies on your makari heritage, limiting the effect to yourself but allowing you to cast it more easily than a common mage; you can target only yourself with the spell, but you can Cast the Spell as a free action if you’re within a body of water when you cast it.
name: River Adaptation

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Scarlet Strands](/Feats.aspx?ID=6845) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gnome" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=617" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 39

**Prerequisites**
[Kijimuna Gnome](/Heritages.aspx?ID=372) heritage

</column>

---

The innate magic in your blood turns your signature crimson tresses into more than just a stylish coiffure. If you pluck three strands of your bright red hair and spend 1 minute braiding them together, they magically transform into a strong, 50-foot, crimson rope. This rope can hold 1,000 pounds—great for lashing down sails in a storm, rappelling down a cliff to a hidden treasure, or tying up a Minkaian criminal with a sizable bounty on her head. You can have only one hair rope in existence at a time; if you braid a second, your first rope unravels back into three hairs.

Your hairs can also form a net to catch fish or foes. Once per day, you can cast 4th-rank [_web_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2045) as an innate primal spell, which takes the form of a crimson fishing net. You must have a hand free to pluck a few strands of your hair that you throw as part of the spell. The hairs regrow when the spell ends.
name: Scarlet Strands

    level="1"
    right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Shore Gift](/Feats.aspx?ID=5354) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Merfolk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=761" />
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=670" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=676" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 38 <sup>2.1</sup>

</column>

---

Using old magic, you slip off your tail like an item of clothing and walk on two feet, resembling a humanoid ancestry, usually [human](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=6) but possibly [elf](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=2), [half-elf](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=7), or something stranger. You're still recognizably yourself, as the Shore Gift doesn't change your upper body. While transformed, you lose your swim Speed from your ancestry (though you might still have a swim Speed from other sources) but gain a land Speed of 25 feet.

 Using the Shore Gift also counts as creating a disguise when using [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388), and your transformation automatically defeats Perception DCs to determine if you're a normal member of whatever ancestry you appear to be; only creatures actively rolling Perception to examine you might notice the disguise. You can remain in your alternate form indefinitely and can shift back to your merfolk form by using this action again.
name: Shore Gift

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Poppet" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=418" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 49

**Frequency**
Once per 10 Minutes

**Prerequisites**
[Tsukumogami Poppet](/Heritages.aspx?ID=383) heritage

</column>

---

You bestow some of your own life energies to mend damage. You touch a non-magical object of 2 Bulk or less, or a magical object of 1 Bulk or less, and you restore Hit Points to the target equal to twice your level. You lose as many Hit Points as the target regained. This direct transfer of vitality means that no effects apply that would increase the Hit Points the target regains or decrease the Hit Points you lose. This transfer also ignores any temporary Hit Points you or the target have. You can’t reduce your Hit Points below 1 using Solidarity. You can’t replace lost pieces or repair an object that has been completely destroyed.

**Special** If you have the [Minuscule Mentee](/Feats.aspx?ID=6580) feat, you can use Solidarity to heal your familiar.
name: Solidarity

[Annotate Composition](/Feats.aspx?ID=4610) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Bard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=546" />
<trait label="Exploration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=66" />
<trait label="Linguistic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=101" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 105 <sup>2.0</sup>

</column>

---

By putting composition to paper, you can create a source of stirring words or song that others can read and understand. You spend 10 minutes and 1 Focus Point to transpose a composition spell on a special scroll that you or another creature can later activate. This composition spell must take a single action to cast. If the chosen composition spell requires a Performance check as part of the casting, the GM rolls this check as a secret check when you annotate your score. If you have fortissimo composition or lingering composition, you can also use one of those spells to modify the annotated composition, provided the annotated composition can benefit from the modification. The GM rolls the secret Performance check. If you do, you spend an additional Focus Point, even if the secret check fails.

Any creature that can read the language you used when annotating your composition can Activate the Item by spending a single action, which has the concentrate trait. This produces the effects of the composition as though the activating creature had Cast the Spell.

A composition you create this way loses its power the next time you make your daily preparations. While the composition is in your possession, you can render it inert using a single action that has the concentrate trait. You can’t regain the Focus Points you spent to create the annotated composition until it is activated or loses its magic.
name: Annotate Composition

>
[Blade of the Heart](/Feats.aspx?ID=7036) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=590" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 94

**Archetype** [Starlit Sentinel](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=275)

**Prerequisites**
[Starlit Sentinel Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7033)

</column>

---

The bonds of the heart are stronger than any steel, more powerful than any magic. You plunge your transformed weapon into the heart of a willing adjacent ally, where it phases harmlessly into their body. As you pull the weapon out, your ally’s heart inscribes one of the following weapon property runes on your weapon: [corrosive](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2834), [flaming](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2838), [frost](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2839), [shock](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2847), [thundering](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2850), or [vitalizing](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2852). The first time you use Blade of the Heart with a given ally, the GM should decide which rune best represents your shared relationship (such as elegant frost for a respected mentor or brash thundering for a boisterous sparring partner); thereafter, each time you use Blade of the Heart with that ally, you draw the same rune. This rune lasts for as long as you remain in sentinel form and counts toward your maximum limit of runes as normal.

At 16th level, you draw the greater version of the rune instead.
name: Blade of the Heart

Reddish ash stains your ikon, impossible to clean off. Every time you exhale, a tinge of red and a scent of spiced smoke float upon your breath. The imbued ikon gains the following ability.

Transcendence—Mark the Center <actions string="Single Action" /> (transcendence) You hold a hand to your lips and exhale, releasing enchanted red ash in a 15-foot cone. The ash clings to the vital areas of each enemy in the area for 1 minute. When a creature marked by the ash is hit and dealt damage by a Strike, it takes an additional 4d6 precision or vitality damage, then its mark ends. <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Chain Infusion](/Feats.aspx?ID=4197) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Infusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=503" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 23 <sup>2.0</sup>

</column>

---

The elemental matter in your blast keeps reconstituting itself to travel onward, no matter how many bodies it collides with. If your next action is an [Elemental Blast](/Actions.aspx?ID=2125) and it hits, attempt a new ranged Elemental Blast from the target against a different creature that's within the blast's range, measuring from the creature you hit. You can keep chaining the blast in this way each time you hit. Your multiple attack penalty applies normally to any blasts in the chain after the first. You can make up to five blasts total, but you can't target the same creature more than once. Roll damage only once and apply it to each creature you hit. (If you start with a melee blast, you still add your Strength to only that blast, not the successive ranged blasts.)
name: Chain Infusion

</title>

<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Rage" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=680" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

---

You open yourself to attacks so you can respond in turn. Until your rage ends, you are [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58), and damage rolls against you gain a +2 circumstance bonus. If a creature hits you, that creature is off-guard to you until the end of your next turn. If you hit it before the end of your next turn, you gain temporary Hit Points equal to your Constitution modifier, or double that on a critical hit. These temporary Hit Points last until the end of your rage.

>
[Command Attention](/Feats.aspx?ID=6301) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=541" />
<trait label="Aura" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=542" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=590" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=647" />
<trait label="Visual" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=727" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 194 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Archetype** [Celebrity](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=245)

**Prerequisites**
[Celebrity Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6298)

</column>

---

You command the attention of all around you with style, ensuring their gaze falls only upon you until the end of your next turn. Whenever a creature in a 30-foot emanation around you attempts a saving throw against a different visual effect, it gets a result one degree of success better than it rolled. This is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) effect. When an enemy within the aura attempts to use a visual effect that involves focusing its attention on a particular creature (such as a medusa’s Focus Gaze), it must succeed at a Will save against your [class DC](/Rules.aspx?ID=23) or [spell DC](/Rules.aspx?ID=2293), whichever is higher, in order to target any creature except you. Allies in the aura can attempt to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) even if they don’t have cover, as you are continually providing a distraction.
name: Command Attention

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=89" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 289

**Archetype** [Palatine Detective](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=306)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Palatine Detective Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7557)

</column>

---

Using various implements and esoteric methods, you can attempt to remove a curse from an unfortunate victim. It takes 10 minutes to perform these rites on a willing creature, who must remain within your reach the entire time. Attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=3280) one [curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=566) afflicting the creature; your counteract rank is half your level rounded up, and you use either your [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) modifier as your counteract modifier. If the afflicted creature or the individual who placed the curse on the afflicted creature is the target of your active investigation through [Pursue a Lead](/Actions.aspx?ID=2811), you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to this counteract check. If the curse comes from a cursed item or other external source, a success indicates that the target creature can rid itself of the cursed item, but it doesn’t remove the curse from the item.
name: Cursebreaker

<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />

</column>

---

You merge with the blossoms sprouting from you and disperse, becoming a visible cloud of blossoms and petals. You’re amorphous. You lose any item bonus to AC and all other effects and bonuses from armor, and you use your proficiency modifier for unarmored defense. You gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) to physical damage equal to half your level and are immune to precision damage. You can’t cast spells, activate items, or use actions that have the attack or [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) trait. You gain a [fly Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2350) of 10 feet. You can remain in this form for up to 1 minute. You can [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) this effect.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 99

**Archetype** [Fan Dancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=276)

**Prerequisites**
[Fan Dancer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7039); [Twirling Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=7046)

**Requirements**

---

You’re practiced in using your fans to spin with dizzying speed. [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=2370) an opponent’s space, and then [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) that opponent. If this second Tumble Through and Strike are successful, you can repeat these actions a third time against a third opponent.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=812" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 67 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Archetype** [Demolitionist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=118) (Level 12)

</column>

---

You can throw bombs at just the right trajectory to create especially large and powerful explosions. When you throw an [alchemical bomb](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=7) and that bomb has the [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) trait, you can have the splash damage affect all creatures within 10 feet of the target instead of 5 feet. If you do, you gain a status bonus to the bomb's splash damage equal to your Intelligence modifier. If you have the [bomber](/ResearchFields.aspx?ID=5) 5th-level field discovery, this additional damage applies even if you caused your bomb to deal splash damage equal to your Intelligence modifier instead of the normal amount, allowing your bombs to deal splash damage equal to double your Intelligence modifier.

You've taught your companions to charge directly at an enemy. Your companions with a qualifying unarmed Strike learn the Ferocious Charge activity.

 **Ferocious Charge** <actions string="Two Actions" /> The companion Strides up to twice its Speed in a straight line and makes an antlers, head, or horn Strike. [Fish from the Falls' Edge](/Feats.aspx?ID=7173) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
<trait label="Exemplar" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=839" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=623" />
<trait label="Vitality" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=509" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 38

**Frequency**
once per day

**Trigger**
A living creature within 30 feet would die.

**Requirements**
Your divine spark is empowering one of your ikons.

</column>

---

Seeing your ally fall, you let out a cry, sending your divine spark to them temporarily to keep them from tumbling down the River of Souls. You prevent the triggering creature from dying and restore 5d8 Hit Points to them. The ally is invigorated by the touch of your divine power, gaining a +1 status bonus to their saving throws and AC for 1 round. Your divine spark remains with your ally, preventing you from gaining any of your ikons’ immanence effects until the start of your next turn, when it returns to an ikon of your choice.

requirement: Your divine spark is empowering one of your ikons.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=541" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=606" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Marshal](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=254)

**Prerequisites**
[Marshal Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6351)

</column>

---

You’ve trained in battle formations for a plethora of situations. Choose a formation. Allies within your aura can use their reaction to Stride up to their Speed and take a place in the chosen formation. Allies can’t benefit from this movement if there isn’t room for them in the chosen formation. If there are more eligible allies than there are available spaces in the chosen formation, you choose which allies benefit.

**Line** Your allies gather adjacent to you and each other to form a straight line in a direction of your choosing. 

**Wedge** Your allies gather into any space that would be covered by a 15-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386) originating from you in a direction of your choosing. 

**Cluster** Your allies gather into any space that would be covered by a 15-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) in an aura around you.
name: Form Up!

[Ghost-path Epiphany](/Feats.aspx?ID=7091) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 114

**Archetype** [Cultivator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=278)

**Prerequisites**
[Cultivator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7085); you aren't [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517)

</column>

---

Deviating from the orthodox path, you tread an inauspicious descent littered with flowers of death; this heretical choice will, in time, earn you the enmity and fear of more traditional cultivators. You become [sanctified](/Traits.aspx?ID=519) with the [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) trait. You also learn the [_call spirit_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=112) and [_commune_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=114) rituals, which can be used to contact only [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) or entities from the Void or the [Netherworld](/Planes.aspx?ID=36).

When you cast a ritual, you can reduce the number of secondary casters by 1 as you direct decaying fragments of your own soul, felled by your proximity to death, to assist with the ritual. When you do, you must fulfill any requirements for the secondary caster, and you attempt the secondary check normally performed by that secondary caster. You can’t replace a secondary caster who’s the target of the spell (as in the [_atone_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=108) ritual).
name: Ghost-path Epiphany

---

You bathe in the arterial fluids of your enemy, drinking deep of their freed essence to empower your magic and increase your spellcasting efficacy. If your next action is to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) that requires a spell attack roll, you roll the spell attack roll twice and use the better result; this is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) effect. Alternatively, if your next action is to cast a spell that requires the creature damaged by the triggering strike to attempt a save, they roll twice and take the lower result; this is a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effect.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=612" />
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=818" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 110 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Requirements**
Your most recent action was to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395), [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390), or [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393), and you failed but didn’t critically fail.

</column>

---

After your attempt to influence someone goes poorly, you add another bit of information or ask a pointed question, possibly salvaging your previous attempt. Reroll the failed check and use the new result. If the target of the failed check is involved with one of your active investigations, double your investigation bonus from [Pursue a Lead](/Actions.aspx?ID=2811) on the rerolled check. That creature is temporarily immune to Just One More Thing for 1 day.

 You can also use this action if you failed, but didn't critically fail, at a check to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389), [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=2391), [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392), or [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=2394). In this case, rather than spending 1 action, adding Just One More Thing takes you half the amount of time you initially spent on the check, to a minimum of 1 more round.

>
[Klingegeist](/Feats.aspx?ID=7702) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Possession" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=129" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 122

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Ghosts are not permitted for PFS play._

**Archetype** [Ghost](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=177)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Headless Haunt](/Feats.aspx?ID=7699)

</column>

---

Your imprisonment inside a [_final blade_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1094) used to perform countless executions has instilled in you an aptitude for entering and possessing similar sharp implements of murder. You project your mind and incorporeal body into an unattended weapon of 2 Bulk or less that deals slashing damage.

While possessing a blade, you have a space of 5 feet, but you don’t block or impede enemies attempting to move through your space, nor do you benefit from or provide [flanking](/Rules.aspx?ID=2375). You’re trained in the use of the weapon, unless your proficiency was already better, and you can make [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) actions with the weapon as if you were wielding it. You gain a [Fly speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2350) of 30 feet and can only take Strike and [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) actions, which don’t trigger reactions. You have an AC of 18 + your level and the [Hardness](/Rules.aspx?ID=2183) and Hit Points of the weapon you’re possessing, which for most one-handed slashing weapons is Hardness 5 and HP 20. You can’t be [Disarmed](/Actions.aspx?ID=2383), nor can your true body be directly injured except by [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage, which bypasses both the weapon’s Hardness and Hit Points to damage you directly.

If you’re reduced to 0 Hit Points or the weapon you’re inhabiting is [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=60) or [destroyed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=46), you’re immediately ejected from it and [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85) for 1 round. Otherwise, the effect lasts for 10 minutes or until you [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) it.
name: Klingegeist

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 83

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**
[Resurgent Maelstrom Hybrid Study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=9)

**Requirements**
You’re wielding an improvised weapon.

</column>

---

You pour energy into an improvised weapon, speeding its destruction to grant it power. The overloaded energy grants your improvised weapon the effect of the _[astral](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2832)_, _[corrosive](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2834)_, _[extending](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2836)_, or _[frost](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2839)_ rune for 1 minute, after which the item is destroyed. If the item has a Hardness greater than your level, or if it's an artifact, cursed item, or other item that's difficult to break or destroy, it is not destroyed, and this ability only lasts until the end of your turn.

This effect doesn't count against the number of property runes a weapon can have based on its potency rune, but a given weapon can only have one application of Maelstrom Flow at a time.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 291

**Archetype** [Razmiran Priest](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=307)

**Prerequisites**
[Razmiran Priest Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7566); Expert in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37)

</column>

---

You have reached the 12th Step and been instructed in greater secrets of [Razmir’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=357) doctrine. You can [Craft](/Rules.aspx?ID=2634) your [Razmiri mask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3592) out of [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2920) or upgrade your existing mask to a silver one in the same time it takes to Craft one made of iron . A silver Razmiri mask grants a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389) or [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390), is a 10th-level item, and gains the following activation in addition to that possessed by the standard mask.

**Activate—Call Upon Razmir’s Mercy** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Frequency** three times per day; **Effect** Exhorting Razmir to purge impurities from your target, you lay hands on a creature within reach and cast [_cleanse affliction_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1467) as an [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) spell with a spell rank equal to half your level. Unlike a normal _cleanse affliction_ spell, this doesn’t reduce the stage of the affliction; instead, if the counteract check is successful, the [affliction’s](/Rules.aspx?ID=2389) stage is temporarily reduced by 1 and its effects are suppressed for 24 hours, after which the affliction resumes in full force. If the target would have been required to attempt additional saves against the affliction during the 24 hours it was suppressed, they must attempt all of those saving throws as soon as the 24-hour duration ends. This could mean that the target saves successfully and it is as if the affliction were truly healed, or it could mean that the affliction returns and advances multiple stages all at once.
name: Mask of The 12th Step
prerequisite: Razmiran Priest Dedication; Expert in Crafting

This feat can be imbued in either a single ikon with multiple copies, such as one produced by the shadow sheath or with the [Twin Stars](/Feats.aspx?ID=7156) feat, or two separate ikons (bypassing the normal limit per ikon feat). **Immanence** As long as you hold one ikon, the other will return to find its partner. **Transcendence—Rejoin in Flight** (transcendence) You throw your weapon ikons to either side of a creature, and they seek each other out, converging on the target. Make two thrown Strikes against a target within the first range increment of both your weapon ikons. This counts as two attacks toward your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn’t increase until after you’ve made both attacks. The target is flanked for both attacks (typically making it off guard against both attacks). If both Strikes hit, the target also takes an additional die of weapon damage. The weapons then return to your hand.
name: Mated Birds in Paired Flight

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mythic Containment](/Feats.aspx?ID=7301) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 84

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

You infuse a receptacle, such as a normal bag, sack, or box, with mythic power, transforming it into a prison into which you can command a creature. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320), and attempt a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39), or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) check at mythic proficiency against the Will DC of a creature within 30 feet to trick, convince, or command it into entering the receptacle. The receptacle can hold a creature of any size, and the creature enters the receptacle if your check is successful. The creature is [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77), is [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1, and has to hold its breath or start [suffocating](/Rules.aspx?ID=2439). A creature trapped in the receptacle can attempt to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296); use the skill you used to lure the creature into the bag for the DC, and calculate the DC using mythic proficiency. The trapped creature is automatically freed after 1 minute, but you can spend an additional Mythic Point as a free action to prolong the duration of the containment for an additional minute when it would expire.
name: Mythic Containment

[Open the Blazing Eye](/Feats.aspx?ID=7565) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 289

**Archetype** [Palatine Detective](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=306)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Palatine Detective Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7557)

</column>

---

Thanks to your diligence in the study of divine and occult mysteries, you can focus to temporarily attain a perception beyond the ordinary. A lightless flame appears in the center of your forehead. For 1 minute, you gain the benefits of a [_see the unseen_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663) spell. In addition, when you attempt a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) during this time against a creature about which you could [Recall Knowledge](/Rules.aspx?ID=2638) using [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46), the attack ignores circumstance penalties to the attack roll and any [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) required due to the target being [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) or [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79).
name: Open the Blazing Eye

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Druid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=583" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Sorcerer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=824" />
<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />

---

With a complex gesture, you call upon the primal power of your spell to overcome enemies’ resistances. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell, the spell ignores an amount of the target’s resistance to acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic damage equal to your level. This applies to all damage the spell deals, including persistent damage and damage caused by an ongoing effect of the spell, such as the wall created by wall of fire. A creature’s immunities are unaffected.
name: Overwhelming Energy

[Pact of the Nightblossom](/Feats.aspx?ID=7449) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=662" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 46

**Archetype** [Pactbinder](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=189)

**Prerequisites**
[Pactbinder Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3822)

</column>

---

You've sworn a pact with Jenway Nightblossom of the Synod of Truth in Dreams, a talented oneiromancer and pactbinder. Through your connection to her, you're able to divine your dreams for wisdom, and they're protected from interference. You're immune to [_nightmare_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1615). During your daily preparations, if you slept and were able to dream, you learn a helpful piece of advice about your future activities, as [_read omens_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1647).

 As payment, Jenway established a permanent telepathic connection to you that functions whenever you sleep or dream. Whenever you learn something significant, Jenway learns it the next time you sleep. You can withhold information, but you lose the benefits of Pact of the Nightblossom until you relent and allow Jenway to learn it.
name: Pact of the Nightblossom

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 81 2.1 **Archetype** [Wild Mimic](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=226) **Prerequisites** [Wild Mimic Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5515); you have attempted a saving throw against a creature’s petrifying gaze or a similar ability or have identified a creature with such an ability in combat --- Either by witnessing or surviving the petrifying stare of a [medusa](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3096) or similar creature, you have learned to petrify those you lock eyes with. You stare at a creature you can see within 30 feet. The creature attempts a Fortitude save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. You must wait 1d4 rounds before using this ability again. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected and temporarily immune to your Petrifying Gaze Mimicry for 24 hours.
**Success** The creature is [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) for 1 round.
**Failure** The creature is slowed 1 for 1 round and [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) for 1 round or until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296).
**Critical Failure** The creature is slowed 2 for 1 round and immobilized until it Escapes.
name: Petrifying Gaze Mimicry

[Plant Shape](/Feats.aspx?ID=4744) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Druid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=583" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 133 <sup>2.0</sup>

**Prerequisites**
[leaf order](/DruidicOrders.aspx?ID=2) or [Untamed Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=4713)

</column>

---

You can take the shape of a plant creature. If you don't have untamed form, you can cast [_plant form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1637) once per day, heightened to the same rank as your highest-rank druid spell slot.

If you do have untamed form, add the shapes listed in plant form to your untamed form list, and whenever you're polymorphed into another shape using untamed form, you gain resistance 5 to poison.
name: Plant Shape

    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Primal Howl](/Feats.aspx?ID=4745) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Druid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=583" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 133 <sup>2.0</sup>

**Prerequisites**
[Incredible Companion (Druid)](/Feats.aspx?ID=4737)

</column>

---

Your companion can let out a howl laced with your primal magic. It gains the following advanced maneuver, in addition to any advanced maneuvers it already knows. 

**Primal Howl** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** Your animal companion screeches and howls, empowered with natural magic. All creatures in a 30-foot cone take 1d6 sonic damage for every 2 levels your companion has, with a basic Fortitude save against your spell DC. Creatures that fail become [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) 1, and creatures that critically fail become frightened 2. The fright is an [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), and [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effect.
name: Primal Howl

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 97 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Prerequisites**
blessed armament

</column>

---

Your blessed armament radiates power, further enhancing your chosen weapon. When you choose the weapon for your blessed armament during your daily preparations, add the [_astral_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2832) and [_brilliant_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2833) property runes to the list of effects you can choose from. If you're [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517), also add the [_holy_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2842) rune, and if you're [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521), also add the [_unholy_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2851) rune.

 In addition, you can change the rune you've selected for the day to a different rune from your list as a 10-minute activity that has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), and [exploration](/Traits.aspx?ID=595) traits. Changing the rune doesn't restore abilities that can be used only a limited number of times, such as Holy Healing for the _holy_ rune.
name: Radiant Armament

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 141 1.1 **Frequency** once per 10 minutes **Prerequisites** [bones mystery](/Mysteries.aspx?ID=14) or [lore mystery](/Mysteries.aspx?ID=18) --- You roll a handful of bones to learn (or perhaps influence) the future course of events. Roll 1d4 and use the corresponding result below. Whenever you Roll the Bones of Fate, any effects from a previous usage immediately end.
**1 Good** You or an ally within 30 feet can roll twice on your next attack roll or skill check, taking the higher result. This is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) effect.
**2 Bad** One creature you are observing within 30 feet must succeed at a Will save against your spell DC; on a failure, the target must roll twice on their next attack roll or skill check that takes at least one action to perform, taking the lower result. This is a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effect.
**3 Mixed** You gain the benefits of rolling both a 1 and a 2.
**4 Cursed Possibilities** Your attempts to meddle in the forces of prophecy bring dire consequences for all. Every creature within 30 feet of you when you perform the augury rolls twice on their next attack roll or skill check that takes at least one action to perform; if the highest number rolled is odd, they take the lower result, and if the highest number rolled is even, they take the higher result. If they took the lower result, this effect has the misfortune trait for them, and if they took the higher result, it has the fortune trait.
name: Roll the Bones of Fate

<title

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Scroll Adept](/Feats.aspx?ID=5040) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=735" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 203 <sup>2.0</sup>

</column>

---

During your daily preparations, you can create two temporary scrolls containing arcane spells from your spellbook. Each scroll must be of a different spell rank, and both spell ranks must be 2 or more ranks lower than your highest-rank spell. Any scrolls you create this way become non-magical the next time you make your daily preparations. A temporary scroll has no value if sold. As normal for a scroll, these are consumable items of light Bulk, and someone holding the item in one hand can Cast the Spell from it if it’s on their spell list, using their spell attack modifier and spell DC. Scrolls are detailed fully on page 262 of GM Core.

If you have master proficiency in spell DC, you can create three temporary scrolls during your daily preparations, and if you have legendary proficiency, you can create four temporary scrolls.
name: Scroll Adept

[Seal of the Golden Dragon](/Feats.aspx?ID=7102) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 117

**Archetype** [Familiar Sage](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=279)

**Prerequisites**
[Familiar Sage Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7095); [Golden Dragon's Bounty](/Feats.aspx?ID=7100)

**Trigger**
You would take [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), or [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) damage.

**Requirements**
Your familiar has the resistance ability and is adjacent to you.

</column>

---

Your familiar coils around you, protecting you with its magical resistance. You gain the benefits of your familiar’s [resistance](/Familiars.aspx?ID=122) ability until the start of your next turn. If your familiar has any upgrades to this ability, such as [major resistance](/Familiars.aspx?ID=117), you gain them as well. Once per day, if your familiar’s resistance is a different damage type, your familiar’s resistance ability changes to the appropriate type. If you already have resistance of the same type, choose the higher of the two.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Wardens of Wildwood</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #201: Pactbreaker](/Sources.aspx?ID=241) pg. 80

**Archetype** [Verduran Shadow](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=312)

**Prerequisites**
[Verduran Shadow Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7606); Master in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49)

**Trigger**
A creature targets you with an [attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=540) and you can see the attacker.

</column>

---

You sense how an incoming attack moves through ambient primal energy, predicting how best to dodge. The triggering attack targets your [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) DC instead of your AC. Though this allows you to avoid taking penalties to your AC, it doesn’t remove any conditions or other effects causing such penalties. For example, an enemy with sneak attack would still deal extra damage to you for being [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58), even though you wouldn’t take the –2 circumstance penalty when defending against the attack.
name: Sense the Strike
prerequisite: Verduran Shadow Dedication; Master in Survival

**Frequency**
once per round

[Shield Warden](/Feats.aspx?ID=4807); blessed shield, champion's reaction

An enemy’s attack against an ally matches the trigger for both your [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) reaction and your champion’s reaction.

When you shield your ally against an attack, you call upon your power to protect your ally further. You use the Shield Block reaction to prevent damage to an ally and also use your champion's reaction against the enemy that attacked your ally.

**Special** If you have an ability that gives you an additional reaction you can use to Shield Block or use your champion's reaction, you can use it for Shield of Reckoning.

prerequisite: Shield Warden; blessed shield, champion's reaction

>
[Spear of Doom](/Feats.aspx?ID=7264) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=701" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 67

**Archetype** [Warrior Of Legend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=286)

**Prerequisites**
[Warrior Of Legend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7261)

**Requirements**
An enemy hit you with an attack dealing the same damage type as your cursed weakness within the last round, and you are [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) 1 or greater.

</column>

---

The conditions for your doom have been met, and you brace yourself for a battle that will see you either live to fight another day or die a legend. You enter the spear of doom stance. While in this stance, as long as the enemy who triggered your cursed weakness is within your reach, you can Strike them as a reaction whenever they succeed or critically succeed at an attack against you. You gain an additional reaction immediately and at the start of each of your subsequent turns that can only be used to make [Reactive Strikes](/Feats.aspx?ID=5832) against that opponent, or to make the [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) granted by this stance.

While in spear of doom stance, your cursed weakness is equal to your level instead of half your level.

[Spy's Countermeasures](/Feats.aspx?ID=7731) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 171

**Archetype** [Lion Blade](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=319)

**Prerequisites**
[Lion Blade Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7724)

**Trigger**
You succeed at a save against a [detection](/Traits.aspx?ID=574), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), or [scrying](/Traits.aspx?ID=689) effect

</column>

---

You’ve learned how to analyze and fake your responses to the most common magic used against spies. You can attempt to identify the effect via [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=2365) using the magical tradition skill of the effect or [Espionage Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41), even if you didn’t notice the spell being cast.

If you successfully identify the triggering effect, and it would normally fail or have no effect, you can make the caster of the triggering effect think the effect or spell succeeded. If they would obtain a result, such as receive a piece of information, you decide what that result is. If the effect would influence you to take certain actions, you can make it appear as if you were affected and attempt to play along; if the effect normally establishes a mental link, it functions normally, but you can disregard any commands you receive through the link.
name: Spy's Countermeasures

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 115

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

At this stage of cultivation, your body is as much spirit as flesh. While still fettered to the physical realm, your form flourishes without needing conventional food or drink, and your natural healing now rivals that brought by scalpel and suture.

You become [sanctified](/Traits.aspx?ID=519) with the [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) trait. When you perform the [Subsist](/Actions.aspx?ID=2368) downtime activity, you can use [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) for the skill check (instead of the skills normally associated with your environment). If you do so, this activity gains the [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) trait as you subsist on ambient qi within your environment’s dew-laden air and create shelter from solidified emanations of qi.

Additionally, when you [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=2621), you can also [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=2399) at the same time. If you do so, you can use Occultism for checks to Treat Wounds and disregard the need for a [healer’s kit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2727); this activity gains the vitality trait as you circulate healing qi through your own body or transfuse your ally with healing qi.
name: Three Pecks of Dew

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Druid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=583" />
<trait label="Sonic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=147" />
<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />

---

Your lightning splits the air, generating a booming shock wave. If your next action is to Cast a Spell that has the electricity trait or deals electricity damage, has no duration, and requires creatures to attempt a saving throw, the force of the spell’s lightning creates a thunderclap, in addition to its other effects. Each creature that failed its Reflex save against the spell is deafened for 1 round, and those who critically failed are also knocked prone.

[Trampling Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=6294) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=606" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 193 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Archetypes** [Cavalier](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=244), [Mammoth Lord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=170) (Level 12)

**Prerequisites**
[Cavalier Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6286)

**Requirements**
You are riding a mount that has a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) using its legs (claw, talons, hoof, etc.).

</column>

---

You urge your mount to charge into the fray, trampling all enemies who stand in your path. You command your mount to [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) up to double its Speed (or to [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310), [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312), or [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381), if it has the corresponding movement type), moving through the spaces of any foes in your path up to one size smaller than your mount. Your mount deals the damage of one of its melee [Strikes](/Rules.aspx?ID=2895) to each creature whose space you move through, with a basic Reflex save against your mount’s [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) DC. On a critical failure, the creature also becomes off-guard until the end of your next turn. Roll the damage only once. You can damage a given creature only once during this movement.

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Trial by Skyfire](/Feats.aspx?ID=6072) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cursebound" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=800" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=604" />
<trait label="Oracle" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=817" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 141 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Prerequisites**
[cosmos mystery](/Mysteries.aspx?ID=15) or [flame mystery](/Mysteries.aspx?ID=16)

</column>

---

Your lips murmur as you portend a great disaster, one you hope you survive. A rain of blazing bolts begins to fall from the heavens in a 10-foot emanation, centered on you, that deals 2d6 fire damage to all creatures in the emanation at the end of each of your turns (basic Reflex save); you can't exclude yourself from the emanation. The skyfire persists for 1 minute; while you can't [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) it, you can suppress the effect for 1 round with a [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) action. The rain of fire is suppressed if you fall [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95). If you become [cursebound](/Traits.aspx?ID=800) 3 or 4 at any point during Trial by Skyfire's duration, the emanation increases to 15 feet and the damage increases to 4d6.
name: Trial by Skyfire

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 84

**Requirements**
You’re wielding a [shield](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=12) or a weapon with the [parry](/Traits.aspx?ID=667) trait.

</column>

---

You’re the bulwark that doesn’t break. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320), and [Raise a Shield](/Actions.aspx?ID=2316) or position the required weapon to parry; for the next minute, whenever you Raise a Shield or position a weapon to parry (including when you first use this ability), all allies you can see gain the shield or weapon’s circumstance bonus to AC. When your shield is raised or your weapon is positioned to parry while this effect is active, enemies treat all squares within your reach as [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366). When using the [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) reaction, after the block is complete, you can attempt a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with a [shield bash](/Weapons.aspx?ID=395) or an attached weapon on the required shield (such as a [shield boss](/Weapons.aspx?ID=396) or [shield spikes](/Weapons.aspx?ID=397)) against an adjacent enemy at mythic proficiency.

The first time each round an enemy misses you with a melee Strike while your weapon is positioned to parry, you can Strike them with that weapon at mythic proficiency as a reaction.

<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=606" />

---

With a quick use of brute force, you remove an obstacle and take a calculated shot as part of the same motion. Attempt to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382) one adjacent creature, then make a ranged Strike with a bow or crossbow you're wielding. The Strike is made at the same multiple attack penalty as the Shove or Trip attempt, and this activity counts as one attack when calculating your multiple attack penalty.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=534" />
<trait label="Light" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=640" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 113

**Prerequisites**
[aloof firmament hybrid study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=7); [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755)

**Requirements**
Your Spellstrike is charged, and you're wielding a one-handed weapon in the sword group.

</column>

---

Honed through 10,000 battles, your sword’s mere light can shatter ambitions and break armies. Make a melee [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755) with a sword, with a spell that isn’t a [cantrip](/Traits.aspx?ID=550) or [focus](/Traits.aspx?ID=511) spell. Countless copies of your sword, made of light, fall around you, dealing damage equal to double the spell’s rank to each creature within a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) of the target, excluding you and the target of the Spellstrike. The damage is of the same type dealt by your sword Strike and is treated as [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2916) and [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2920).

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Unstable Concoction](/Feats.aspx?ID=5790) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Additive" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=795" />
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=812" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 67 <sup>1.1</sup>

</column>

---

You can mix a wondrous yet volatile liquid into an [alchemical](/Traits.aspx?ID=528) [consumable](/Traits.aspx?ID=564) if it has an initial effect that uses dice. You [increase the size of any dice](/Rules.aspx?ID=2305) for the item's initial effect by one step. For instance, you could increase damage from a [moderate alchemist's fire](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3287) to 2d10 or healing from a [moderate elixir of life](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3308) to 5d8+12. Because this affects only initial dice, it wouldn't increase unarmed attack damage from a [bestial mutagen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3315), [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) from an [acid flask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3286), and the like. When this item is activated, the creature activating it must succeed at a DC 10 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) or take acid damage equal to the item's level.
name: Unstable Concoction

>
[Vermilion Threads](/Feats.aspx?ID=7083) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=534" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 113

**Prerequisites**
[Arcane Cascade](/Actions.aspx?ID=756); [unfurling brocade hybrid study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=8)

**Trigger**
You use Arcane Cascade.

</column>

---

Your Arcane Cascade sends threads to the four directions, creating a web of strings dyed by your skill and your enemies’ blood. The web fills a 15-foot [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385) centered on you and is [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366). You can ignore the difficult terrain, and the strings can support your weight, allowing you to walk on them as though you were benefiting from [fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312). 

The web lasts for 1 minute but ends early if your Arcane Cascade ends or you leave the web.

If you [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) from a spell slot while in the web, the strings glow red until the beginning of your next turn, dealing damage equal to the spell’s rank to any creature other than you that moves through the web. The damage occurs at the end of the creature’s movement, with a basic Reflex save against your spell DC. A creature can take this damage only once each round.
name: Vermilion Threads
prerequisite: Arcane Cascade; unfurling brocade hybrid study

[Apocalypse Rider Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7304) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Destiny" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=838" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 107

**Archetype** [Apocalypse Rider](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=287)

</column>

---

In the darkest hour of the night, a fearsome and terrible steed arrives as a gift from a powerful daemonic patron. You gain an apocalypse mount, which is loyal and follows your commands as long as you work to spread death and destruction. Your apocalypse mount can be any [mature animal companion](/Rules.aspx?ID=2117) with the [mount](/Feats.aspx?ID=2113) special ability, though it is obviously touched by daemonic forces. Choose whether your apocalypse mount is a [nimble](/AnimalCompanions.aspx?Advanced=true&ID=7) or [savage](/AnimalCompanions.aspx?Advanced=true&ID=8) animal companion. During an encounter, even if you don’t use the [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400) action, your apocalypse mount can still use 1 action on your turn to [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) or [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306).

You also gain the anathema “You forswear any plans to cheat death or build something that will last beyond your own death.” If you break this anathema, you lose access to abilities granted by this archetype until you atone or make amends.

**Special** If you already have an animal companion with the mount special ability, it becomes your apocalypse mount as daemonic energies infuse its form. In such a case, one of your companion’s unarmed attacks increases one die size.
name: Apocalypse Rider Dedication

[Archfiend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7320) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Destiny" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=838" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 110

**Archetype** [Archfiend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=288)

</column>

---

Driven by your Calling, you've begun to make plans for your own personal realm from whence you're destined to rule over an army of fiends. Name your realm and describe its eventual appearance. Whether it contains raging hellfire, ponds of caustic acid, or banks of poisonous fog, your realm should be marked by distinctive [terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=3108). Select one of the following damage types associated with your realm's environmental dangers: [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), or [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669). This is your realm's damage type. You gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) to the selected damage type equal to half your level. If you already have resistance to this damage type, increase your resistance by 5. The certainty of your will is such that you can temporarily bring forth a portion of your realm into this world. You gain the Manifest Realm ability. Other feats allow you to further manipulate your manifested realm. 

Manifest Realm <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** You corrupt the surrounding area into a manifestation of your realm in a 20-foot-radius burst centered on you. Your manifested realm counts as [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) for your enemies, and your enemies take a –1 penalty to Fortitude saving throws while in your manifested realm. You can Sustain your manifested realm once per round on subsequent rounds, and if you do not, the radius of your manifested realm is reduced by 5 feet. Your realm remains manifested for a maximum of 1 minute, and you can Dismiss your manifested realm. If your manifested realm's radius is ever reduced to 0 feet or if you move beyond 100 feet from the borders of your manifested realm, your manifested realm is automatically Dismissed.
name: Archfiend Dedication

Whether it contains raging hellfire, ponds of caustic acid, or banks of poisonous fog, your realm should be marked by distinctive [terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=3108). Select one of the following damage types associated with your realm's environmental dangers: [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), or [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669). This is your realm's damage type. You gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) to the selected damage type equal to half your level. If you already have resistance to this damage type, increase your resistance by 5. The certainty of your will is such that you can temporarily bring forth a portion of your realm into this world. You gain the Manifest Realm ability. Other feats allow you to further manipulate your manifested realm. 

Manifest Realm

---

>
[Ascended Celestial Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7331) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Destiny" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=838" />
<trait label="Fortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=612" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 115

**Archetype** [Ascended Celestial](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=289)

</column>

---

Your Calling has driven you to perform mortal deeds that will result in your ascension to the ranks of celestials. You’re headstrong and determined and hardly waver in your resolve; once per hour, you can roll twice and use the higher result on a Will saving throw. If you ever become [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63), rather than attack wildly, you become stubbornly immobile, wasting all your actions until the condition ends. 

Additionally, you emanate a nimbus of light. You shed [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) in a 30-foot radius (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) to the next 30 feet). You can suppress or reestablish this light as a single action that has the concentrate trait. As long as your nimbus is active, all allies in the area of your nimbus gain a +1 status bonus to saves against fear. You gain the Bless Ally action.

**Bless Ally** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612), [mythic](/Traits.aspx?ID=835)) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes; **Requirements** Your nimbus is active; **Target** a willing ally within the bright light of your nimbus; **Effect** Your radiance grants an ally some of your celestial grace. That ally can roll twice and use the higher result for the next Will save they attempt before the beginning of your next turn.
name: Ascended Celestial Dedication

[Assassinate](/Feats.aspx?ID=6261) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 186 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Archetype** [Assassin](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=239)

**Prerequisites**
[Assassin Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6257)

**Requirements**
You have designated a mark using Mark for Death and are completely [unnoticed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=98) by your mark.

</column>

---

You strike with one swift movement, trying to instantly slay your mark. Make a Strike against your mark. If you hit, your mark takes an additional 6d6 precision damage with a basic Fortitude save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. If the mark critically fails, it dies unless its level is higher than yours. Regardless of the result of its save, the creature is temporarily immune to your Assassinate for 1 day.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Destiny" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=838" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 118

**Archetype** [Beast Lord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=290)

**Prerequisites**
a [mature animal companion](AnimalCompanions.aspx) or an [advanced construct companion](ConstructCompanions.aspx)

</column>

---

Your Calling has united your destiny with a [companion](/Traits.aspx?ID=558), harnessing a connection between you that links your minds, hearts, and souls. Choose a companion that qualified you for this feat as your united companion. Your united companion increases its Intelligence modifier to +0 or by 1 if its Intelligence modifier is greater than +0. It gains the ability to understand a language that you know and can communicate with you, but only you can understand your companion when it speaks, as it uses chirps, grunts, or other noises to convey its meaning. If you or your united companion are conscious and within 30 feet of each other and either must attempt a saving throw against a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effect, both you and your united companion attempt the saving throw. The target of the effect uses the best result; this also applies if both you and your united companion must attempt a saving throw against the same effect.
name: Beast Lord Dedication
prerequisite: a mature animal companion or an advanced construct companion

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=541" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=676" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 189 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Frequency**

**Prerequisites**
[Beastmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6267); Call Companion

</column>

---

You quickly call in a primal projection of a non-active companion to provide the companion’s support benefit.
