---

You can apply two different [infused](/Traits.aspx?ID=797) [injury](/Traits.aspx?ID=635) [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) to the same weapon, though not to a piece of ammunition. Each poison's level must be 2 or more levels lower than your level. You have to apply the two poisons individually. Once you've applied both, the poisons merge into a double poison that uses the lower of the two poisons' DCs and number of stages. This double poison is [virulent](/Traits.aspx?ID=726) only if both poisons were virulent. Combine the effects of each stage of the poison on any creature affected by it. For each stage of the poison, use the effects of both poisons and the longer interval for that stage among the two poisons.

Your movements are like that of a dragon weaving a serpentine path between your enemies and allies. Using your fans, you slice the air and create a path of least resistance, allowing you to move across the battlefield with an ethereal grace. You Stride, your movement doesn’t trigger enemy reactions, and any allies you pass within 5 feet of can immediately use their reaction to Stride, moving in the same direction. Allies must end their movement as close as possible to you or another ally who benefited from this ability. During Dragon’s Journey, ally movement doesn’t trigger reactions.

Your blows hamper both a foe’s mobility and cognitive functions by focusing first on their lower extremities and then their head. Then, make another Strike against the same creature. If that Strike hits and deals damage, the creature is also [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 until the end of your next turn.     pfs="Standard"
>
[Earworm](/Feats.aspx?ID=4623) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Bard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=546" />
<trait label="Exploration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=66" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 106 <sup>2.0</sup>

</column>

---

By endlessly repeating a motif, you implant a memorable song that repeats over and over again in your allies’ heads, preparing them to respond to it later. Choose a [composition](/Traits.aspx?ID=559) cantrip and spend 10 minutes repeating a melody, chant, speech, series of motions, or a similar performance that embodies that cantrip. This activity gains the traits appropriate to the type of performance. You implant the earworm within all allies who can see or hear you (as appropriate for the type of performance) for the entire activity.

Once you’ve created the earworm, you can attempt a [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) check as a free action to activate it. This check uses the highest Will DC of the earworm’s targets present at the time of activation. On a success, you cast the cantrip on all allies who learned the earworm and can perceive your performance; on a failure, the earworm is corrupted and lost. Because it is based on the earlier repetitions, you can’t use further free actions like [_lingering composition_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1769) or [_fortissimo composition_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1766) to modify the activated earworm. Allies forget the earworm after it is activated, if you spend 10 minutes to implant another earworm, or during your next daily preparations, whichever comes first.
name: Earworm

    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Flamboyant Leap](/Feats.aspx?ID=6172) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Swashbuckler" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=825" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 168 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Prerequisites**
[Flamboyant Athlete](/Feats.aspx?ID=6146)

**Requirements**
You are capable of using a [finisher](/Traits.aspx?ID=322).

</column>

---

You stylishly leap and deliver a powerful finisher. Make a [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298), [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377), or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378) and attempt one single-action finisher at any point during your jump; the finisher can't be one that includes other movement, such as Mobile Finisher. Immediately after the finisher, you fall to the ground if you're in the air, even if you haven't reached the maximum distance of your jump. If the distance you fall is no more than the height of your jump, you take no damage and land upright. When attempting a High Jump or Long Jump during a Flamboyant Leap, determine the DC using the Long Jump DCs, and increase the maximum distance to double your Speed, rather than just your Speed.

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 125 <sup>1.1</sup>, [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 130 <sup>2.0</sup>

**Archetype** [Wrestler](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=270) (Level 14)

**Prerequisites**
[Wrestler Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6446)

**Requirements**
You have a foe [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90). 

</column>

---

Your ability to control your own qi empowers you to pressure other creatures into resuming their true forms. Attempt an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) a [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670) effect currently affecting your target. If the target is somehow under the effect of multiple polymorph effects, you can choose which one to attempt to counteract, or the GM chooses randomly if the separate effects aren't obvious. The target is then temporarily immune for 1 day.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs=""
>
[Guarded Domain](/Feats.aspx?ID=7347) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 119

**Archetype** [Beast Lord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=290)

**Prerequisites**
[Beast Lord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7345)

</column>

---

You and your united [companion](/Traits.aspx?ID=558) have elected to become guardians of a particular location or domain. If you spend 1 week of downtime within a settlement or natural area with a 5-mile radius, you and your companion can become guardians of the area and consider it to be your guarded domain. Your guarded domain remains under your protection until you spend more than 1 month outside of your domain, after which you must spend another week of downtime to re-attune to your guarded domain. You can only have one guarded domain at a time, and selecting a new guarded domain immediately ends your protection over the previous guarded domain. 

If a creature has been in your guarded domain for at least 1 hour while you or your companion are also inside your domain, you or your companion can attempt to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=2391) about the target by spending 1 minute communing with the land or its residents. You attempt this check at mythic proficiency.

In addition, once per day as a 3-action activity you can spend a Mythic Point to instantly teleport yourself and your united companion to a location you are aware of within your domain. This is a [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) effect.
name: Guarded Domain

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=606" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 207 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Archetype** [Mauler](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=256)

**Prerequisites**
[Mauler Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6368)

**Requirements**
You’re wielding a non-[finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602)  melee weapon in two hands.

</column>

---

You smash the ground with your weapon, knocking nearby creatures to the ground. Choose a square within your reach, including your own space. If there’s an enemy in the chosen square, you can [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) that enemy with your two-handed weapon. Regardless of whether you attempted a Strike, you then attempt to [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382) every enemy in the chosen square plus each square adjacent to that square, ignoring Trip’s requirement that you have a hand free.

Hammer Quake counts as three attacks toward your [multiple attack penalty](/Rules.aspx?ID=2289), but the penalty doesn’t increase until after you’ve made the Strike, if any, and all the Trip attempts.

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Impossible Riposte](/Feats.aspx?ID=6173) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Swashbuckler" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=825" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 169 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Prerequisites**
Opportune Riposte

</column>

---

Your ripostes can deflect attacks back at their source. You can use Opportune Riposte with a trigger of “A foe outside of your reach critically fails an attack roll against you” in addition to its usual trigger. When you use Opportune Riposte with this new trigger against a ranged attack, your Strike deflects some of the triggering effect back toward its source. Compare the result of your attack roll to the AC of the triggering foe. On a hit, you deal the normal amount of damage for your Strike, but the damage type changes to that of the triggering attack. For instance, if you used Opportune Riposte to deflect a [_blazing bolt_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1450), your Strike would deal fire damage instead of its normal damage type.
name: Impossible Riposte

In the world of drama, the finale of any performance doesn’t have to be the end, and for you, this now extends to life itself. Instead of gaining the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition and falling [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95), you regain a number of Hit Points equal to 10 + your level + your Constitution modifier.

>
[Manipulate Realm](/Feats.aspx?ID=7323) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 111

**Archetype** [Archfiend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=288)

**Prerequisites**
[Archfiend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7320)

</column>

---

Thanks to your continued belief in your ultimate transformation, you have learned greater control over your manifested realm. If you spend a Mythic Point when you Manifest your Realm, you can use the Drain Realm, Spread Realm, and Unleash Realm free actions.

 **Drain Realm** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Trigger** Your previous action was to Sustain your manifested realm; **Requirements** Your manifested realm has a radius of at least 10 feet; Effect You siphon power from your manifested realm to bolster your physical form. Decrease your manifested realm's radius by 10 feet. You regain a number of Hit Points equal to your level and each of your Strikes made before the end of your turn deal an additional 1d8 damage of your realm's damage type.

 **Spread Realm** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Trigger** Your previous action was to Sustain your manifested realm; **Effect** Your manifested realm further corrupts more of your surroundings. Increase your manifested realm's radius by 10 feet.

 **Unleash Realm** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Trigger** Your previous action was to Sustain your manifested realm; **Effect** You punish those who transgress upon your realm. An enemy within your realm takes 4d8 damage of your realm's damage type with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher.
name: Manipulate Realm

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 291

**Archetype** [Razmiran Priest](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=307)

**Prerequisites**
[Razmiran Priest Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7566); Master in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37)

</column>

---

You have ascended to the 15th Step and stand among the greatest of [Razmir’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=357) priests. You can [Craft](/Rules.aspx?ID=2634) your [Razmiri mask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3592) out of gold or upgrade your existing mask to a gold one in the same time it takes to Craft one made of iron. A gold Razmiri mask grants a +3 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389) or [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390), is a 14th-level item, and gains the following activation in addition to those possessed by the standard and silver masks. 

**Activate—Call Upon Razmir’s Wrath** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cry out to Razmir to reveal his fiery wrath, as he did upon the unbelievers at Melcat. You cast [_sunburst_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1707) as an 8th-rank [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) spell, but for [undead](/MonsterTemplates.aspx?ID=3) targets the spell has the [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631) trait.

**Prerequisites**
[Prophet of Kalistrade Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7680)

</column>

---

Kalistrade teaches that setbacks are only temporary and that perseverance is a treasured virtue. When you fail, but not critically fail, at a [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) or Mercantile [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) check to Earn Income at a specific task and are allowed to continue working at that task on subsequent days, you can choose to attempt the skill check again the next day. If you succeed, you get a critical success and continue to earn that amount on further days spent working at the task, if the task lasts that long.

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 68 1.1 --- Basic mutagens that affect your mind and thoughts can make you communicate telepathically, protect you from being detected, or let you communicate with anyone. While you're affected by one of the listed mutagens, you get an additional benefit.
  • **[Cognitive Mutagen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3316)** You also gain the mutagen's item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40), [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45), [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46), and [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) checks. In addition, you can communicate telepathically with creatures within 60 feet with whom you share a language. The communication is two-way once you establish it, so a creature you contact can also communicate with you.
  • **[Serene Mutagen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3320)** [Detection](/Traits.aspx?ID=574), [revelation](/Traits.aspx?ID=686), and [scrying](/Traits.aspx?ID=689) effects of 9th rank (or 17th level) or lower detect nothing from you or your possessions and auras. For instance, [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485) would still detect other magic in the area, but not any magic on you.
  • **[Silvertongue Mutagen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3321)** Ignore circumstance penalties you would take to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40), and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) checks. In addition, your words transcend linguistic barriers; everyone listening to you speak hears your words as if you were speaking in their own language (though you don't actually speak that language, nor does this ability allow you to understand any additional languages).
**Special** If you can be under the effects of multiple mutagens (with the [mutagenist](/ResearchFields.aspx?ID=7) greater field discovery, for example), you get all relevant benefits.
name: Mutant Innervation

<column gap="tiny">

---

Your mystery holds unknowable depths of magic not always associated with the divine. You can have one spell in your spell repertoire not on the [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579) spell list, in addition to spells you've added to your spell list from abilities like divine access. You cast that spell as a divine spell. You can swap which spell you add and from which tradition as you could any other oracle spell, but you can't use this feat to have more than one spell from another tradition in your spell repertoire at the same time.

It will take more than a gathered mass of foes to take you down. You gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) equal to your level to damage dealt by [swarms](/Traits.aspx?ID=707), [troops](/Traits.aspx?ID=367), and creatures who occupy the same space as you. In addition, you can briefly menace large groups of enemies to step aside. You gain the Overawe Crowd activity.

**Overawe Crowd** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Requirements** You are sharing the same space as a [swarm](/Traits.aspx?ID=707) or are adjacent to a [troop](/Traits.aspx?ID=367); **Effect** Spend 1 Mythic Point and attempt an [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) check at mythic proficiency against the Will DC of the required swarm or troop. On a failure, the target Strides in a direction of your choosing and you move along with it. On a success, the target Strides twice in a direction of your choosing and you can decide whether or not to move along with it. No matter the result, the target is stunned 1 and temporarily immune to your Overawe Crowd for 24 hours.

---

You’ve sworn a pact with a psychopomp bent on the destruction of all undeath. You gain an imprecise deathsense that can detect undead creatures up to 60 feet away. Additionally, whenever an undead creature is destroyed within 60 feet you gain temporary Hit Points equal to its level that last for 1 minute.

 In exchange, the psychopomp requires that you never aid in the creation or conquest of an undead creature. You must also seek out and put to rest any mindless or destructive undead creatures you come across.
name: Pact of the Death Hunter

---

You’ve sworn a pact with a powerful fey creature that longs to see the wonders of the Universe. You gain the Fey Jump ability. In exchange, you can no longer see the moon or stars as the fey steals those wonders from your eyes, and you must gaze at the empty sky for at least 10 minutes each night. If you do not, the fey revokes your benefits for the next day. If you go a week without gazing, the fey revokes your benefits until you atone. 

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Fey Jump;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) You jump through the First World for a brief second, teleporting up 60 feet away to an empty space you can see. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you’re carrying it in an extradimensional container—the action is lost.
name: Pact of the Fey Paths

The aura lasts until the end of your next turn, but the familiar can Sustain it up to 1 minute.

<trait label="Prediction" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=674" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Time Mage](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=191) (Level 16)

---

You spend 10 minutes in contemplation to uncannily predict how events will play out. Choose a particular goal or activity you plan to engage in within 1 week, or an event you expect might happen within 1 week. You analyze whether it's likely to come to pass, learning whether it's highly likely, somewhat likely, somewhat unlikely, or highly unlikely. You also gain a piece of advice suggesting a course of action you or your allies could take that might make the chosen event more or less likely, whichever you prefer. The GM determines the likeliness of the event and the piece of advice you learn.
name: Plot the Future

<traits>

<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 109

**Archetype** [Red Mantis Assassin](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=271)

**Prerequisites**
[Red Mantis Assassin Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6519)

**Requirements**
You are wielding a sawtooth saber in each hand.

</column>

---

You've mastered the signature assassination style of the Red Mantis. Attempt to [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390) an enemy within 30 feet. If your Feint is successful, when you use Prayer Attack on subsequent turns you automatically make the target flat-footed against your melee attacks for that turn without rolling a check to Feint, so long as you remain visible to the target and the target remains within 30 feet of you. If you use your Prayer Attack against a different target, you must attempt to Feint the target normally.

 When you use Prayer Attack, your next successful Strike with a sawtooth saber that turn deals 2d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) to the target.

requirement: You are wielding a sawtooth saber in each hand.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />

**Archetype** [Apocalypse Rider](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=287)

**Prerequisites**
[Apocalypse Rider Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7304)

</column>

---

You spoil the food and water nearby, even within your foes’ bodies. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320). Enemies within 60 feet of you must succeed at a Fortitude save against your class DC or spell DC (whichever is higher) or become [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1. You also cause edible food to rot and potable water to turn brackish within the area. Choose a number of [potions](/Traits.aspx?ID=672) or alchemical [elixirs](/Traits.aspx?ID=589) within the area equal to your key attribute modifier and attempt a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) against each of them using [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) at mythic proficiency. Your counteract rank is half your level. If you succeed, the elixir or potion spoils and becomes a mundane item.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=647" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 132

**Archetype** [Godling](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=293)

**Prerequisites**
[Godling Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7392)

</column>

---

You open your senses so the prayers of mortals can better reach your ears. You gain a +1 status bonus to checks to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302), but only when attempting to ascertain hopes, prayers, wishes, and other strongly held desires of the target. You gain an even greater sense of your hierophant's prayers, which grants you a constant [_status_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1690) as a constant [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spell targeting your hierophant. The spell has unlimited duration and functions at any range, included across planar boundaries, and [counteracting](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) the spell merely suppresses it until your next [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575), though it automatically ends if the creature stops being your hierophant. 

You gain the ability to cast [_breath of life_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1456) once per day as a 5th-rank divine innate spell. You can cast this spell only on your hierophant, and the spell has unlimited range (your status spell typically alerting to you to when your hierophant would die).
name: Receive Prayers

When you successfully use Counterspell to counteract a spell that affects targeted creatures or an area, you can turn that spell’s effect back on its caster. When reflected, the spell affects only the original caster, even if it’s an area spell or it would normally affect more than one creature. The original caster can attempt a save and use other defenses against the reflected spell as normal.

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 101 **Archetype** [Wandering Chef](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=277) **Prerequisites** [Morning Side Dishes](/Feats.aspx?ID=7054) --- You can create dishes that reflect the food sources endemic to your environment and medicinal food techniques utilizing the cycle of the five elements. When you create alchemical food from Morning Side Dishes during your daily preparations, you can add one elemental benefit of your choice to each of the items. This benefit comes in addition to any other effect of consuming the item. Each element has an immediate benefit and a +3 item bonus to certain saves that lasts for 1 hour after the food is consumed. The item bonus increases to +4 if the alchemical item is 18th level or higher.
  • **Wood** Remove one source of [persistent bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86). For 1 hour, gain a +3 item bonus to saves against [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578) and [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) effects.
  • **Fire** Reduce the [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) condition by 1. For 1 hour, gain a +3 item bonus to saves against being [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) or [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76)
  • **Earth** Reduce the [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) condition by 1. For 1 hour, gain a +3 item bonus to saves against being [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71).
  • **Metal** Reduce the [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) condition by 1. For 1 hour, gain a +3 item bonus to saves against being stupefied.
  • **Water** Reduce the frightened condition by 2. For 1 hour, gain a +3 item bonus to saves against [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66) or drained.
name: Regional Specialty

>
[Release Me!](/Feats.aspx?ID=7360) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=606" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 123

**Archetype** [Broken Chain](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=291)

**Prerequisites**
[Broken Chain Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7357)

**Requirements**
An enemy has you [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90).

</column>

---

Your retribution against one who would detain you is swift and dangerous. Make a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) against the creature who has you [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90). You can still make this attack even if you are restrained, though not if you are wielding a two-handed weapon. Unless your Strike is a critical failure, you can then attempt a check to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296). If the creature who has you grabbed or restrained is the target of your [Ultimatum of Liberation](/Actions.aspx?ID=2993), you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to this check. Both the Strike and the Escape count toward your multiple attack penalty, but it doesn’t increase until you’ve made both rolls.

    pfs=""
>
[Rites of Liberation](/Feats.aspx?ID=7361) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 123

**Archetype** [Broken Chain](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=291)

**Prerequisites**
[Broken Chain Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7357)

</column>

---

You learn the [freedom](/Rituals.aspx?ID=178) ritual. If you spend an additional [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) while casting it, you reduce its casting time to 1 hour, and both the primary and secondary casters attempt their corresponding skill checks at mythic proficiency. If you would critically fail the ritual, you fail instead. Additionally, you gain the [_unimpeded stride_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1806) and [_word of freedom_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1807) domain spells. These are focus spells, granting you a focus pool of 2 Focus Points or expanding that pool if you already have one. You can Refocus while you meditate on the concepts of freedom and liberty. (For more on focus spells, see [here](/Rules.aspx?ID=2228).)
name: Rites of Liberation

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Witch" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=734" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 190 <sup>2.0</sup>

---

You can adapt your patron’s power to transform other creatures into forms more befitting their behavior or your whims. Your familiar learns [_cursed metamorphosis_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1479), even if _cursed metamorphosis_ isn’t on your tradition’s spell list. By spending 10 minutes in communion with your familiar, you can replace one spell of 6th-rank or higher you’ve prepared in one of your witch spell slots with a _cursed metamorphosis_ spell of the same rank.
name: Rites of Transfiguration

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=735" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 204 <sup>2.0</sup>

</column>

---

You divert some of your spell’s energy into an unstable runic array. If your next action is to Cast a Spell that deals damage, has no duration, and affects an area, a glowing magic circle appears in a 5-foot burst within that area. At the beginning of your next turn, the circle detonates, dealing 1d6 force damage per rank of the spell to all creatures within the circle, with a basic Reflex save against your spell DC. If the spell dealt a different type of damage, the circle deals this type of damage instead (or one type of your choice if the spell could deal multiple types of damage).
name: Secondary Detonation Array

---

You fold your spell into a seed. If your next action is to Cast a Spell using 1 action or 2 actions, the spell instead plants itself in an adjacent square. You must make all decisions regarding the spell at the time you cast it. Within the next 10 minutes, you can direct your sown spell to sprout and produce the spell’s effects as a reaction, which is triggered when a creature enters the sown spell’s space or a square adjacent to it. You can have only one sown spell at a time, and if you don’t trigger the spell within 10 minutes, it dissipates and the spell is lost. A creature can notice the sown spell with a successful Perception check against your spell DC.

</column>

---

Your aura links your friends together with mystic strands. While you’re in this stance, an ally within your spellsurge aura can treat any other ally within the aura as the point of origin for a spell they cast, calculating range and cover from the other creature’s space instead of their own. This allows all allied creatures within your spellsurge aura to act as though they’re in touch range of each other since each creature is in touch range of itself. Additionally, while you’re in this stance, an ally casting a spell that targets only the caster can have that spell affect any other ally within your _spellsurge_ aura instead.

</title>

<traits>

**Prerequisites**
[Sunder Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=5859)

</column>

---

You can focus your superstition to break the magic of an item, in addition to destroying freestanding spells and those active on creatures. When you Sunder a Spell, you can instead attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) either an unattended magic item or one of your target's magic items. If your counteract attempt succeeds, the item becomes a mundane item of its type for 10 minutes. If you target an [artifact](/Traits.aspx?ID=537), an [intelligent item](/Traits.aspx?ID=636), or a similarly particularly powerful item, your counteract attempt automatically fails.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=645" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 205 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Archetype** [Marshal](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=254)

**Prerequisites**
[Marshal Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6351)

**Trigger**
An ally succeeds at a ranged  [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) against an opponent in your weapon’s first range increment.

**Requirements**
You have a ranged or thrown weapon in hand.

</column>

---

You capitalize on your ally’s attack and use the opportunity to secure a blow of your own, adding to the oncoming barrage. Make a ranged [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with a –2 penalty against the opponent targeted by the triggering attack. This Strike doesn’t count toward your [multiple attack penalty](/Rules.aspx?ID=2289), and your multiple attack penalty doesn’t apply to this Strike. If this Strike is successful, combine the damage from the attack with the damage from your ally’s attack for the purpose of [resistances](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) and [weaknesses](/Rules.aspx?ID=2317).

requirement: You have a ranged or thrown weapon in hand.

<traits>

**Prerequisites**

---

You have turned into a plant version of yourself, gaining the [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125) trait and losing traits inappropriate for your new form (typically [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=91)). You also gain the Verdant Rest action.

**Verdant Rest** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) You turn into a tree or other noncreature plant. This has the effect of using [_one with plants_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1618) to turn into a plant, except that your AC is 30. You can [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=74) this effect to turn back. If you rest for 10 minutes in this form in natural sunlight, you recover half your maximum Hit Points. If you take your daily rest in this form, the rest restores you to maximum Hit Points and removes all non-permanent [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10), [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13), [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3), and [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) conditions, as well as all poisons and diseases of 19th level or lower.

You fall through your own kinetic gate, leaving behind an effigy of flame and reappearing majestically near another fire. You instantly transport yourself, and any items you're wearing and holding, from your current space to a clear space within 120 feet you can observe that's adjacent to an open flame or a creature taking [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). If this would bring another creature with you—even if you're carrying it in an [extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67) container—the action fails.

 A whorl of fire surrounds you in a 5-foot emanation either before you depart or after you arrive. Each creature in the area takes 4d6 fire damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC.

---
**Level (+3)** The fire damage increases by 1d6.

You and your united companion can share each other’s spaces. When you do so, both you and your united companion provide [lesser cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=2372) to one another. You and your united companion also count as being adjacent to one another when sharing each other’s spaces. A target is automatically [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) against the first [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) each round each of you and your united companion make while sharing one another’s spaces; this benefit also applies if you are [mounted](/Traits.aspx?ID=411) on your united companion.
name: We are One

>
[Whirling Blade Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=6037) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=656" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=701" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 126 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Prerequisites**
[Monastic Weaponry](/Feats.aspx?ID=5979)

</column>

---

You enter a mindful stance that creates a deep connection between you and your monk weapons, allowing you to manipulate them with your qi, even at a distance. All melee [monk](/Traits.aspx?ID=656) weapons you wield with the [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602) trait gain the [thrown 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=711) trait (unless they already have the thrown trait with a greater range).

 Once you've made a thrown Strike with such a weapon, you can use the precision of your throw to make additional strikes with it, even from a distance. Start from the space of the previous Strike's target to determine the range increment and whether the new target has cover. At the end of your turn, the thrown weapon flies directly back to you in a straight line. If a solid barrier blocks its path, it falls to the ground after hitting the barrier.
name: Whirling Blade Stance

**Source** [Pathfinder #194: Cult of the Cave Worm](/Sources.aspx?ID=209) pg. 81 **Archetype** [Worm Caller](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=208) **Prerequisites** [Worm Caller Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=4357) --- You take on the form of a purple worm or transform into a humanoid-worm hybrid, retaining your own head but with a worm's body, transforming into a Huge battle form. You must have enough space to expand into or the ability is lost. While in this form, you gain the [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=9) trait. You can Dismiss the form. You gain the following statistics and abilities regardless of which battle form you choose:
  • AC = 20 + your level. Ignore your armor's check penalty and Speed reduction.
  • 40 temporary Hit Points.
  • [Darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415).
  • One or more [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) melee attacks specific to the battle form you choose, which are the only attacks you can Strike with. You're trained with them. Your attack modifier is +25, and you use the listed damage. Melee attacks are Strength based (for the purpose of the [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) condition, for example). If your unarmed attack modifier is higher, you can use it instead.
  • [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) modifier of +30, unless your own modifier is higher.
You also gain specific abilities based on the type of monster you choose:
  • **Purple Worm** Speed 40 feet, burrow 30 feet, swim 20 feet; **Melee** jaws ([deadly 2d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+15 piercing; **Melee** stinger ([agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d12+15 piercing plus 2d6 [persistent poison](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29); **Melee** body ([reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)) **Damage** 1d10+13 bludgeoning
  • **Hybrid** Speed 40 feet; **Melee** stinger ([agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d12+15 piercing plus 1d6 [persistent poison](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29); **Melee** body ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 1d10+13 bludgeoning; **Hybrid Caster** You retain the ability to speak, and can cast spells as long as they don't have somatic or material components.

[You Can't Hide From Us](/Feats.aspx?ID=7349) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 119

**Archetype** [Beast Lord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=290)

**Prerequisites**
[Beast Lord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7345)

**Requirements**
Your united [companion](/Traits.aspx?ID=558) made a successful [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) against a creature this round.

</column>

---

When you and your [companion](/Traits.aspx?ID=558) attack together, you can ensure that escape is but a whispered dream. [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) the same creature that your united companion hit. If your Strike is successful, the targeted creature has been marked for death by you and your companion and can’t become [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) or [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) to you and your companion for 1 minute or until it moves more than 60 feet away from either you or your companion, whichever comes first. If the triggering creature is under an effect or spell that would normally grant it this condition, you can immediately attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) the effect. Your counteract rank is half your level rounded up, and your counteract check modifier is equal to the higher of your class DC –10 or spell DC –10.

>
[You Can't Keep Us Down](/Feats.aspx?ID=7363) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=623" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 124

**Archetype** [Broken Chain](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=291)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Broken Chain Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7357)

</column>

---

Seeing your allies falter, you fill their hearts with your unbreakable hope, rousing them to stay in the fight. All allies within 60 feet that are [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69), or [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) and [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=99), are healed a number of Hit Points equal to three times your level. Then, all allies within 60 feet that are [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88) may stand up as a free action that does not provoke reactions.
name: You Can't Keep Us Down

>
[Cloud Jump](/Feats.aspx?ID=5133) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 253 <sup>2.0</sup>

**Prerequisites**
Legendary in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3)

</column>

---

Your unparalleled athletic skill allows you to jump impossible distances. Triple the distance you jump on a successful [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378) (so you could jump 90 feet with an Athletics result of 30). When you successfully [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377), use the distance jumped and distance limit for a Long Jump but don’t triple the distance.

 You can jump a distance greater than your Speed by spending additional actions when you Long Jump or High Jump. For each additional action spent, add your Speed to the distance limit.
name: Cloud Jump

[Craft Anything](/Feats.aspx?ID=5139) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 254 <sup>2.0</sup>

**Prerequisites**
Legendary in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)

</column>

---

You can find ways to craft just about anything, despite restrictions. As long as you have the appropriate Crafting skill feat (such as Magical Crafting for magic items) and meet the item’s level and proficiency requirements, you ignore just about any other requirement, such as being of a specific ancestry or providing spells. If a requirement adds to the item’s cost, you must still pay it (including castings of spells that themselves have a cost). You can’t ignore requirements of special items that have exclusive means of access and Crafting, such as artifacts. The GM decides whether you can ignore a requirement.
name: Craft Anything

You’re so immersed in divine scripture that you find meaning and guidance for any situation in your texts. Spend 10 minutes Deciphering Writing on religious scriptures of your deity or philosophy while thinking about a particular problem or conundrum you face, and then attempt a Religion check (DC determined by the GM). If you succeed, you unearth a relevant passage, parable, or aphorism that can help you move forward or change your thinking to help solve your conundrum.

---

Your skill with languages and codes is so great that you can decipher information with little more than a quick read through a text. You can Decipher Writing using Society while reading at normal speed. If you slow down and spend the full amount of time that’s ordinarily required and roll a success, you get a critical success; if you critically succeed while spending the normal amount of time, you gain a nearly word-for-word understanding of the document.
name: Legendary Codebreaker

Legendary in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49)

---

You know the wilderness so well that you can help your party travel through it with ease. When you are setting the path for your party through wilderness terrain, your party gains a +10-foot circumstance bonus to its Speed for the purpose of calculating the party's [travel Speed](/Actions.aspx?ID=2441), your party's travel Speed doesn't decrease in [difficult terrain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2336), and greater difficult terrain halves your party's travel Speed instead of reducing it to a third. This doesn't increase your party's Speed during an encounter or allow your party to ignore difficult terrain during an encounter.
name: Legendary Guide

---

Your fame has spread throughout the lands. Creatures who have any listed skill in Society have heard of you and usually have an attitude toward you one step better than normal, depending on your reputation and the creature’s disposition. For instance, if you’re well-known for cruel and demanding behavior, creatures might be intimidated by you, rather than be friendly toward you. When you Earn Income with Performance, you attract higher-level audiences than your location would allow, as audiences flock to see you. For instance, rulers and angels might travel to your small tower in the woods to hear you perform. Typically, this increases the audiences available to your level or by two levels, whichever is higher.

Attempt an Intimidation check against the Will DC of a living creature within 30 feet of you that you sense or observe and who can sense or observe you. You understand the common underpinnings of the four traditions of magic and magical essences, allowing you to understand them all through an arcane lens. **Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 98 1.1 **Prerequisites** [Imposing Destrier](/Feats.aspx?ID=5908) --- Guided by your ongoing care, your steed has developed incredible intelligence and skill. The mount you gained with Faithful Steed is now a [specialized animal companion](AnimalCompanions.aspx?Specialized=true). You can select one of the usual specializations or the auspice specialization. A faithful steed with the auspice specialization gains the following benefits.
  • It gains the [celestial](/Traits.aspx?ID=551), [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=600), or [monitor](/Traits.aspx?ID=655) trait—whichever best matches your deity's servitors, and its appearance shifts to look more like those servitors.   • Its Intelligence modifier increases by 2 and its Wisdom modifier by 1.
  • Its proficiency rank in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) increases to expert.
  • It can speak the language associated with your deity's servitors (such as [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115) for celestials, [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114) for demons, or [Requian](/Languages.aspx?ID=34) for psychopomps).
  • Its maximum Hit Points increase by 20, increasing to 25 at 18th level and 30 at 20th level. If the mount has the celestial trait, the extra HP increase by 5, and the mount gains weakness 5 to unholy. If it has the fiend trait, the extra HP increase by 5, and the mount gains weakness 5 to holy.
  • It gains wings that grant it a fly Speed equal to its land Speed.

>
[Bat Around](/Feats.aspx?ID=7350) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 120

**Archetype** [Beast Lord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=290)

**Prerequisites**
[Beast Lord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7345)

</column>

---

Your attack moves a foe into a position that your united [companion](/Traits.aspx?ID=558) can take full advantage of. Make a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) against an enemy. As long as your Strike deals damage, you can attempt an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check to either [Reposition](/Actions.aspx?ID=2379) or [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) the creature you hit. Both attacks count toward your multiple attack penalty, but it doesn’t increase until after you’ve made both attacks. If your Reposition or Shove moves the target and it ends this movement within your united companion’s reach, your companion can Strike the target. Unless it critically fails, your companion can also attempt an Athletics check to Reposition or Shove the creature. These attacks affect your united companion’s multiple attack penalty the same way.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=687" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 176 <sup>2.0</sup>

**Prerequisites**
Legendary in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5)

</column>

---

Your deceptions confound even the most powerful magic that could spy on you. Detection, revelation, and scrying effects pass right over you, your possessions, and your auras, detecting nothing unless the detecting effect has a counteract rank of 10 or higher. For example, detect magic would still detect other magic in the area but not any magic on you, truesight wouldn’t reveal you, locate or scrying wouldn’t find you, and so on.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 116

**Archetype** [Ascended Celestial](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=289)

**Prerequisites**
[Ascended Celestial Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7331)

</column>

---

You imbue a fragment of your divine spark into a weapon, blessing your blade and transforming it into a weapon worthy of the celestial realms. Select one weapon or [handwraps of mighty blows](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3086) when you make your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575). The weapon sheds light like a [torch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2760), deals an additional 1d8 spirit damage, and creatures who wield it gain the weapon’s [critical specialization](/Rules.aspx?ID=2203).

When you critically hit a target with the weapon, the target must succeed at a Fortitude save against your class DC or spell DC (whichever is higher) or be [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1d4 rounds. 

As a single action that has the [concentration](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait, you can hold your hand aloft and call this weapon back to your possession; it immediately teleports into your hand.

While you’re holding this weapon, you can spend 1 Mythic Point as a single action to temporarily grant a blessing to weapons wielded by your allies. Each ally within the [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) of your nimbus when you take this action selects one weapon in their possession. For 1 minute, the selected weapons gain the following benefits: the weapon sheds light like a torch, the weapon deals an additional 1d6 [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage, and creatures who wield the weapon gain the weapon’s critical specialization.
name: Celestial Armaments

Using fantastic acrobatic skill, you can walk for brief stretches across insubstantial surfaces. When you Stride, you can move across water, air, and solid surfaces that can hold only limited weight as if they were normal ground. If you Stride over a trap with a weight-sensitive pressure plate, you don’t trigger it. At the end of your turn, you sink, fall, break fragile surfaces, or trigger traps as normal for your current location.

You can find a loophole in a mental effect to temporarily overcome it. Until the end of your next turn, you ignore a single mental effect. You can suppress a particular effect using Cognitive Loophole only once. You can’t use Cognitive Loophole to suppress an effect you chose to have affect you.

<traits>
<trait label="Cursebound" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=800" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
<trait label="Oracle" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=817" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 143 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Prerequisites**
any oracle mystery

**Requirements**
You have [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1554) or [_harm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1552) as a signature spell and an available spell slot to cast it with.

</column>

---

You use the unstable energy of your [curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=566) to manipulate the most basic of divine magic. You cast a 3-action [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1554) or [_harm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1552) spell, expending the slot as normal. If the spell restores Hit Points to one or more creatures, then one creature healed by this spell regains a number of additional Hit Points equal to 1d8 × your [cursebound](/Traits.aspx?ID=800) value; if the spell damages one or more creatures, then one creature harmed by this spell takes additional damage equal to 1d8 × your cursebound value.

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 128

**Archetype** [Eternal Legend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=292)

**Prerequisites**
[Eternal Legend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7374)

**Requirements**
You are adjacent to a climbable surface at least 10 feet tall.

</column>

---

Seemingly to defy gravity, you use a nearby vertical surface to propel yourself upward and then [strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) downward like the driving rain. [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) up to half your Speed upward on the required surface; if you have a [climb Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2349), you may use your full climb Speed instead. The surface does not need to span the full height of your Stride. You can then either make a ranged Strike at a target within your weapon’s first range increment and land in the space you began (or an adjacent space) without taking [falling](/Rules.aspx?ID=2352) damage, or you can land in a space adjacent to a creature within 10 feet of the required surface without taking falling damage and make a melee Strike against that creature. Either Strike deals an extra two dice of weapon damage. In addition, the target dealt damage by your Strike must succeed at a Fortitude saving throw against your class DC or become [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) 1.
name: Death from Above

**Success** As critical success, but the curse lasts for 1 minute.
**Failure** As critical success, but the curse lasts for 1 round and the target doesn’t gain weakness to spirit damage.
**Critical Failure** The target is unaffected.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 120

**Archetype** [Beast Lord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=290)

**Prerequisites**
[Beast Lord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7345)

**Trigger**
You and your [companion](/Traits.aspx?ID=558) are within 15 feet of each other, and a foe successfully [Strikes](/Rules.aspx?ID=2895) your united companion.

</column>

---

You can protect your [companion](/Traits.aspx?ID=558) from danger with a welltimed attack. You can immediately [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) toward the triggering enemy and can make a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) against them if they would be in the first range increment of your ranged weapon or within your melee [reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=684). If this Strike is successful, reduce the damage to your companion by your level, or twice your level if the Strike was a critical success.
name: Defend Our Union

<trait label="Rage" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=680" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 84 <sup>1.1</sup>

</column>

---

Your blood boils when you take a beating, and you throw caution to the wind to finish the fight. You get a +2 circumstance bonus to attack rolls, a –1 penalty to AC, and a –1 penalty to saves. These bonuses and penalties last until your Rage ends or until you are above half Hit Points, whichever comes first.

<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=676" />
<trait label="Rage" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=680" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 84 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

**Prerequisites**
[Dragon's Rage Wings](/Feats.aspx?ID=5854)

</column>

---

You transform into a ferocious Large dragon, gaining the effects of 6th-rank [_dragon form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1502) except that you use your own AC and attack modifier, you apply your extra damage from [Rage](/Actions.aspx?ID=2802), and the Dragon Breath action uses your class DC. Add the temporary Hit Points from _dragon form_ to any you already have from entering a rage (or any other action with the [rage](/Traits.aspx?ID=680) trait). The action to Dismiss the transformation gains the [rage](/Traits.aspx?ID=680) trait.

 At 18th level, you gain a +20-foot status bonus to your fly Speed, your damage bonus with dragon Strikes increases to +12, and you gain a +14 status bonus to your Dragon Breath damage.

    level="1"

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Forest's Heart](/Feats.aspx?ID=7146) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Animist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=836" />
<trait label="Apparition" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=837" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=701" />
<trait label="Wandering" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=843" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 26

**Requirements**
Your attuned apparition grants Forest [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) or Herbalism Lore as one of its apparition skills.

</column>

---

You adopt a stance that allows your apparitions to channel spiritual energy down through you to inhabit roots, control vines, and command plant-life from the ground you stand on to fight on your behalf. You call forth roots, vines, or other plant growth native to the region and can use them to make unarmed attacks. These deal 4d8 bludgeoning damage, are in the [brawling group](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4), and have the [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602), [grapple](/Traits.aspx?ID=619), and [reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=684) 30 feet traits. Attacks made with these unarmed attacks don’t gain additional damage from [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) runes, but can benefit from the item bonus to attack rolls and [property runes](/Rules.aspx?ID=3168) of [handwraps of mighty blows](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3086) you wear.

<title

    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Free from Bonds](/Feats.aspx?ID=7539) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 281

**Archetype** [Mortal Herald](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=305)

**Prerequisites**
[Flash of Omnipresence](/Feats.aspx?ID=7531)

</column>

---

As a mortal herald, you cannot easily be captured, nor can your allies. If you are [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) when you use Flash of Omnipresence, the creature or effect that is imparting that condition on you takes [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage equal to your level. If you teleport adjacent to a grabbed or restrained ally using Flash of Omnipresence, attempt a [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) check against the hard DC for the level of the creature or effect that is imparting that condition. On a success, your ally no longer has that condition.
name: Free from Bonds

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Fuse Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=6039) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=656" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 126 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Prerequisites**
at least two stances

</column>

---

You have combined two stances into a single stance all your own. When you take this feat, choose two stances you know and combine them into a single fused stance. Give your new fused stance a unique name. When you enter your fused stance, you gain all the effects of both stances, including the requirements and restrictions.

 If the stances both grant special attacks, you gain all those attacks. If a stance restricts you to one particular attack (such as [Crane Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=430)), you must abide by that restriction. If the fused stances have incompatible restrictions, the GM determines which apply, or determines you can't fuse those stances at all.
name: Fuse Stance

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 41 --- Your blood turns a divine gold, shining in moments its spilled and begetting new life. The imbued ikon gains the following effects. **Immanence** If your divine spark remains in your body ikon for 10 continuous minutes, you regrow one damaged or ruined limb or organ.
**Transcendence—Shed the Mortal Skin** (healing, light, transcendence, vitality) Like the serpent, that most ancient of immortals, you shed your skin, revealing a glowing divine form. If you are currently taking persistent fire or acid damage, you immediately end the effect. Until the beginning of your next turn, you shed bright light in a 20 foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) like a torch. The next time you are dealt damage by an enemy before the beginning of your next turn, you shed glowing ichor in a square adjacent to you, and where it hits the earth, a glowing, thorned herb grows. A creature other than you can pluck and consume the herb with an Interact action to regain a number of Hit Points equal to half of the damage you were dealt by the attack that sprouted the herb.
name: Gift of the Immortal Herb

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs=""
>
[Gird Champion](/Feats.aspx?ID=7398) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 132

**Archetype** [Godling](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=293)

**Prerequisites**
[Godling Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7392)

</column>

---

Your will manifests into divine weapons to protect and arm your followers. When you gain this feat, choose one type of weapon with special significance to you, such as a [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386) or a [sickle](/Weapons.aspx?ID=364). This becomes your favored weapon. You and your hierophant both treat this weapon as a simple weapon for the purposes of proficiency. You and your hierophant gain the [critical specialization](/Rules.aspx?ID=2203) effect of your favored weapon and deal an additional 1d6 spirit damage with [Strikes](/Rules.aspx?ID=2895) made with your favored weapon. If one of your current domain spells can deal a type of damage other than [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737), you can choose to match this damage type (for instance, wreathing your weapon in sacred ashes that deal fire damage if you have the [fire](/Domains.aspx?ID=76) domain).
name: Gird Champion

Even a single missile can throw off your enemy’s balance, and more powerful attacks leave it flustered for longer.     pfs=""
>
[Imbue Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=7424) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 139

**Archetype** [Wildspell](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=295)

**Prerequisites**
[Wildspell Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7418)

**Trigger**
Your previous action was to [Cast a Spell](/Rules.aspx?ID=3144).

</column>

---

You pass the energy of your magic onto an ally, allowing another to release the spell. Upon completing the [Casting of a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734), instead of the normal effects of the spell, you imbue the energy of that spell to an ally that’s adjacent to you or within your spellsurge aura. You expend the spell, spell slot, or [Focus](/Rules.aspx?ID=285) Point as normal. At any time during the next hour, that ally can release the energy of the spell with a single action that has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) and [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) traits; they don’t need to expend any spell slots or Focus Points. All attributes of the spell are determined based on your original casting of the spell, including any [spellshape](/Traits.aspx?ID=513) feats used, but the ally is treated as the spellcaster for determining the origin of the spell and for making any choices the spell requires. If the spell must or can be [Sustained](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317), your ally takes the action to Sustain it. You can’t target yourself with this ability. If the spell isn’t released by the ally within 1 hour, the energy dissipates. You can only have one spell imbued at a time; additional uses of this ability cause previously imbued spells to [dissipate](/Rules.aspx?ID=2236) immediately.
name: Imbue Spell

It has a +4 status bonus to hit creatures wearing any type of armor. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 281

**Archetype** [Mortal Herald](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=305)

**Prerequisites**
[Mortal Herald Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7528); Master in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48)

</column>

---

Sometimes your deity requires you to act in the shadows, accomplishing things without drawing attention to yourself— or them. Once per day, when you roll [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) for initiative at the start of a combat, you can choose to be [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83) for 1 minute. If you spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323) while beginning the [Avoid Notice](/Actions.aspx?ID=2622) exploration activity, you are invisible for as long as you continue to Avoid Notice.
name: Invisible Hand
prerequisite: Mortal Herald Dedication; Master in Stealth

<traits>

<trait label="Apparition" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=837" />

All enemies within 40 feet who can see and hear you must attempt a Will saving throw against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. Regardless of the result, a creature is then temporarily immune to Kneel Before the Rightful Heir for 24 hours. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes 3d6 [persistent mental damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86).
**Failure** The creature takes 6d6 persistent [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) damage.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes 6d6 persistent mental damage and is [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) 2 for as long as it’s taking that persistent damage. The persistent mental damage can be ended only if the creature [Drops Prone](/Actions.aspx?ID=2295) in a location that you can see and doesn't Stand until their next turn. An affected creature is aware of this restriction.

[Lead the Pack](/Feats.aspx?ID=6276) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 189 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Archetypes** [Beastmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=241), [Undead Master](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=176) (Level 16)

**Prerequisites**
[Mature Beastmaster Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=6269); you have multiple animal companions

</column>

---

You can have up to two animal companions active at once. However, when you do, it’s slightly more difficult to Command them. If you don’t Command either of your companions, one of the two (your choice) can still use 1 action on your turn to [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) or [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306), per [Mature Beastmaster Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=6269), but not both. When you Command an Animal, either choose one of the companions to take 2 actions, as normal, or else each companion can take 1 action to Stride or Strike. Either way, you can’t Command an Animal to make either companion act again until your next turn
name: Lead the Pack
prerequisite: Mature Beastmaster Companion; you have multiple animal companions

Your ikon gains a pin, stripe, or similar marking showing you as a master of your craft. The imbued ikon gains the following ability. 

**Transcendence—A Challenge for Heroes** <actions string="Two Actions" /> (concentrate, mental, spirit, transcendence) You declare an enemy within 60 feet to be a heroic test. For 1 minute, that enemy deals an additional 10 spirit damage to you with each successful Strike or spell it targets you with. Whenever that enemy deals spirit damage to you, each ally who has the enemy in melee reach can attempt a [Reactive Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2256) against it, even if the ally doesn’t normally have that reaction. If an ally successfully slays the enemy with a Reactive Strike due to this effect, that ally immediately gains temporary Hit Points equal to your level, which persist for 1 minute.
name: Mark of The Sage

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 111

**Archetype** [Archfiend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=288)

**Prerequisites**
[Archfiend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7320)

</column>

---

You have been in contact with a retinue of [fiends](/Traits.aspx?ID=600), brokering all manner of deals so that they may eventually serve you. When you [Manifest your Realm](/Actions.aspx?ID=2986), you can choose to have one such fiend come to your aid. This fiend is a [common](/Traits.aspx?ID=557) fiend of level 11 or lower, which you select when you take this feat. The fiend appears in a place of your choosing within your manifested realm and has the [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=653) trait. They remain for as long as your realm is manifested, until they’re reduced to 0 Hit Points, or until you command them to leave, at which point they immediately vanish and return to their place of origin. 

At 20th level, you can choose a common fiend of level 15 or lower to appear instead when you Manifest your Realm.
name: Marshall Fiendish Forces

Your apparitions share with you the monstrous nature of those creatures who dwell in deep seas or ancient woods. You add [_monstrosity form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1608) to your apparition spell repertoire, allowing you to cast it with your apparition spellcasting.

<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=590" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=647" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Foolish Housekeeping and Other Articles](/Sources.aspx?ID=239)

**Prerequisites**
[Venture-Gossip Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7599)

---

It seems like your knowledge has come in handy after all and you have your enemy at your feet. Pulling out your fan mail, you read your fans' scathing remarks about your enemy to their face, letting them feel just how much everyone hates them and everything that they've done. They hate the way that they walk, they hate the way that they talk.

 Your enemy takes 10d10 mental damage, with a basic Will save. On a critical failure, they're [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the beginning of your next turn and lose all reactions, except to cry, loudly.

>
[My Kingdom, My Blood](/Feats.aspx?ID=7409) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=645" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 136

**Archetype** [Prophesied Monarch](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=294)

**Prerequisites**
[Prophesied Monarch Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7403)

</column>

---

The health of the ruler is the health of the kingdom, and the health of the kingdom is that of its ruler, each bound to the other inextricably. [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305). You can [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310), [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312), or [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type. You then plant your fist or weapon into the ground at your feet, creating a 60-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) in an aura around you that lasts for 1 minute. Whenever an ally within this aura takes damage, you can use your reaction to take half the damage in their stead while they take the remainder. When you take damage through this link, you don’t apply any [resistances](/Rules.aspx?ID=2893), weaknesses, or other abilities you have to that damage; you simply take that amount of damage. Whenever you take damage while this effect is active, an ally within the aura can use their reaction to take half the damage for you in the same manner.

The effect ends immediately if you’re reduced to 0 Hit Points.
name: My Kingdom, My Blood

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Prophesied Monarch](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=294)

**Prerequisites**
[Prophesied Monarch Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7403)

**Trigger**
One of your designated knights is within 15 feet of you and would take damage from an enemy’s [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306).

</column>

---

As your knights devote their lives and swords to you, so too do you return their devotion with your own fierce protection. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320). The knight [Steps](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304) as a free action, and you [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) into the space previously occupied by the knight; this movement ignores [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) and greater difficult terrain. You then take the triggering damage instead. If you have a [shield raised](/Actions.aspx?ID=2316) and have the [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) reaction, you can use it as part of this ability, applying damage to the shield as though you were the original target of the attack. The enemy whose [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) triggered this reaction is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the end of your next turn.

[One with the Spirits](/Feats.aspx?ID=7587) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 294

**Archetype** [Rivethun Invoker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=309)

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**
[Rivethun Invoker Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7581)

**Requirements**
You’re under the effects of Enter Spirit Trance.

</column>

---

The spirits you’ve invoked throughout your life have left behind echoes and spiritual fragments, which you can manifest across your own flesh, temporarily transforming you into something more akin to spirit than mortal. For 1 minute, you gain [fast healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=62) 5 and you become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62). You can’t use this concealment to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404). Your [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) gain the benefits of a [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840) property rune. Whenever you deal damage with a Strike, you can choose to have that Strike deal [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage, rather than its usual damage type.

If you would be knocked [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) or your [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) value would increase while One with the Spirits is active, the spirits revive you at the beginning of your next turn, restoring you to 30 Hit Points. One with the Spirits then immediately ends.
name: One with the Spirits
requirement: You’re under the effects of Enter Spirit Trance.

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Overwhelming Blow](/Feats.aspx?ID=4852) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=601" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 150 <sup>2.0</sup>

</column>

---

You throw your weight into a powerful attack that leaves you vulnerable. Make a melee Strike. This counts as three attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty. If this Strike hits, you get a critical hit. If you roll a critical hit, your weapon or unarmed attack also gains the deadly d12 trait (this replaces any deadly trait it already has). Whether or not you hit, you become stunned 1 and are off-guard until the start of your next turn.
name: Overwhelming Blow

    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Pact of the Rune Dragon](/Feats.aspx?ID=7453) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=534" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 47

**Archetype** [Pactbinder](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=189)

**Prerequisites**
[Pactbinder Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3822)

</column>

---

While the students of Cobyslarni are taught to make pacts with many kinds of dragons, a pact with a rune dragon is somewhat more frequent due to their interest in the accomplishments of various academies. You immediately learn 10 languages chosen from common languages, uncommon languages, and any others the dragon has access to. Additionally, you can [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=2365) at a range of 30 feet as a single action ability with the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait.

 In exchange, the rune dragon requires you to research a topic and send a detailed report each year. Year to year, the dragon may change the interest of your research as they see fit. If you fail to send an appropriately detailed report, you lose this ability unless you spend one week serving the dragon.
name: Pact of the Rune Dragon

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Barbarian" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=813" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=606" />
<trait label="Rage" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=680" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 85 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Requirements**
You are wielding a ranged or thrown weapon that deals piercing damage

</column>

---

Your projectiles are unhindered by flesh and bone. Make a ranged Strike with a ranged or thrown weapon that deals piercing damage against each creature in a 30-foot line (this uses only one projectile despite the number of Strikes). These Strikes ignore all [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=459) granted by creatures. Roll damage only once and apply it to each creature you hit. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but don't increase your penalty until you have made all your attacks.

---

You use clever tactics to mislead your foes as you sneak away. You Sneak while leaving a decoy behind. The decoy acts as the spell mislead, though you aren’t invisible, just undetected. You can continue to concentrate to move your decoy, as with the spell, whether or not you remain hidden throughout the duration. Once you use Perfect Distraction, you need to spend 10 minutes to set up another decoy before you can use it again.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=645" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=647" />
<trait label="Oracle" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=817" />
<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />
<trait label="Visual" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=727" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 143 <sup>1.1</sup>

</column>

---

Your spellcasting is rife with strange lights, mild fumes, and other captivating effects that befuddle your foes. If the next action you use is to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734), any creature that attempts to use a reaction triggered by your Cast a Spell activity takes a –2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls and skill checks rolled as part of the reaction. In addition, if the spell includes a spell attack or requires a saving throw, creatures you hit or that fail their saves are [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72) with you until the start of your next turn.
